The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 1–9:

Lesson No. 231: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 1 to 25

Verses 1 to 8

The surah begins with the two letters Ha and Mim, and after them:

Wal-kitabil-mubin (43:2) is coordinated with them. Allah swears by the letters Ha and Mim and also by the Clear Book. Ha and Mim are themselves letters of this same Book, or the Clear Book is of the same kind as these two letters. In short, this Clear Book is composed of letters of the alphabet, just as such letters are composed. These two letters are of the same kind as the letters found in human languages. They are signs of the Creator of the universe, who created man in this manner and gave him these kinds of sounds. When these letters are mentioned together with the Quran, they carry countless meanings and countless indications and allusions. The oath is sworn to the fact that We made the Quran in this manner, in the Arabic language.

Inna ja'alnahu Qur'anan 'arabiyyan la'allakum ta'qilun (43:3): "We have made it an Arabic Quran so that you may understand." Since the Quran is in their language and they also know its meanings, it is their duty to try to understand it. The Quran is indeed divine revelation, but Allah transmitted it in the Arabic language, because for the call of the Quran Allah chose the Arab society at the beginning, and the bearers of this call first remained the Arabs. This is based on the wisdom to which we have pointed in Surah al-Shura, because Allah knew well the capacities of this trust and of this language, that the Arab nation and the Arabic tongue could convey this call well to other nations. Allah knows where to place the trust of His message and where not to place it.

After this, it is stated what the status of this Quran is in the eyes of the eternal and everlasting Being of Allah:

Wa innahu fi Ummil-kitabi ladayna la'aliyyun hakim (43:4): "And indeed it is inscribed in the Mother of the Book, with Us, exalted and full of wisdom." We do not go into the literal meaning of Umm al-Kitab, whether it refers to the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz) or to Allah's eternal knowledge, because our understanding does not have a complete conception of either the Preserved Tablet or Allah's eternal knowledge. However, from this verse a fundamental truth comes to our knowledge. When we read this verse, "And indeed it is inscribed in the Mother of the Book, with Us, exalted and full of wisdom," it becomes clearly evident to our minds that this Book has great worth in Allah's knowledge and is regarded as a very important document. This principle and general statement is sufficient for us: the Quran is a book of lofty rank and is wise, that is, a book full of wisdom. These two attributes give this Book a personality like a living human being, exalted and wise. And it is exactly so. It is a book as though it has life, and has the qualities of a living personality: the souls that harmonize with it, it walks alongside them. And by its loftiness and wisdom it watches over humanity, guides it, leads it, according to its nature and its characteristics, and it instills in human understanding those values and concepts to which the two attributes, 'Ali (exalted) and Hakim (wise), apply.

Having settled this truth decisively, the people in whose language this exalted and wise Book was revealed should now clearly understand how great an honour Allah has bestowed upon them, and yet they do not appreciate this grace and kindness of Allah. Even so, they turn away from this treasure of wisdom and disparage it. In these circumstances, they deserve that the revelation of this book of wisdom and guidance that comes to them should be stopped altogether. Therefore, their transgression is pointed out here and asked in an interrogative manner: will the fountainhead of guidance and wisdom be closed because of your transgression and your excess beyond all bounds?

Afanadribu 'ankumu ... musrifin (43:5): "Shall We then withdraw the Reminder from you and disregard you, because you are a people who exceed the limits?" This seems very strange, and will remain strange in future too: that Allah gave such importance to a people that He sent a Book for them, in their language. That Book spoke what was in their hearts in accordance with their very nature, reached the depths of their lives, and set out for them the path of guidance; it related the instructive stories of earlier nations and described how the Divine Way (Sunnat Ilahiyyah) dealt with the nations before them. Yet they neglected this Book and turned away from it! Still Allah cares for these people, although He is the Most High, the Most Great, and the Self-Sufficient King.

In this verse there is in fact a terrifying warning: if Allah wills, He can bring an end to this fountain of bounty and wisdom and cut off this mercy upon you, because you are treating this great, wise and exalted Book very badly, and He may deal with you as He dealt with the peoples who passed before you.

Wa kam arsalna ... al-awwalin (43:6) Wa ma ya'tihim ... yastahzi'un (43:7) Fa ahlakna ... mathalul-awwalin (43:8): "How many prophets We sent among earlier peoples! Never did a prophet come to them but they mocked him. Then We destroyed those who were far stronger than these, and the example of earlier peoples has already passed." What are they now waiting for? Allah has destroyed, in response to such conduct, nations far more powerful than them, who likewise mocked messengers and books. Many examples exist.

It is very surprising that these people acknowledged the existence of Allah. They also acknowledged that it is Allah who created the heavens and the earth. Yet after these acknowledgements they did not accept the natural consequences of them, and in the affairs of their lives they did not turn to Allah alone. They associated other beings with Allah, dedicated some of the animals created by Allah to these deities, and they had fabricated the belief that the angels are the daughters of Allah. They made idols of the angels and worshipped them.

Here the Quran presents their acknowledgements and then draws out their natural consequences, and then places them before natural reasoning from which they used to flee. The Quran presents, as examples from among Allah's creations, the animals and the ship, showing how many benefits there are for you in them and what your attitude towards them should be, but it is not so. After this, in the second paragraph, it is explained what justification there is for you to have made the angels the daughters of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 10–14 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 9 to 14

The Arabs believed in God, and they followed the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham). However, what remained among the Arabs was a distorted form of the millat-e-Ibrahimi (the religion of Abraham). Many changes had taken place in it. In place of tawhid (the oneness of God), shirk and other fables had entered it. Nonetheless, they acknowledged the existence of the Creator, because human nature cannot in any case deny that there is a Creator, who is Allah. For no sound-natured person can deny a Creator. And no reasonable person can say that this great and awe-inspiring universe came into being without a Creator. Nor can anyone other than Allah create this universe, because the Creator of this great universe must be even greater and more powerful than it. But they would stop at this point and would not accept the necessary demands of their own belief.

﴿And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ (43:9). It is clear that these two attributes, the Almighty and the All-Knowing, were not the statement of the disbelievers. They only acknowledged that He is Allah; they did not accept the attributes which Islam and the Quran presented, attributes which have a positive effect on their lives, and which govern their lives and this universe simultaneously in practice. They acknowledged Allah merely as the Creator of this universe, and they also acknowledged Allah as their own Creator. But for running life in practice, they had made other beings. This was because they were not acquainted with such attributes of Allah, after which they would have no need of shirk, and the doctrine of shirk would appear to them as hollow and worthless.

The Quran here teaches them this very thing: that the God whom you consider the Creator of the heavens and the earth is also the Almighty and the All-Knowing. He is also All-Powerful, and He is also All-Knowing and All-Aware. Therefore Allah, taking their acknowledgement as a foundation, compels them to the following acknowledgements. In short, He takes them one step further and tells them that after creation, Allah has bestowed this favour upon you:

﴿He it is who made the earth a cradle for you and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided.﴾ (43:10). The fact that Allah made the earth a cradle for man has been understood and depicted by every age of humanity according to the limits of its knowledge. Those who heard this for the first time must also have understood that Allah made the earth suitable so that it is fit for walking upon with their feet. Then it is suitable for agriculture. Then it is suitable for life and vegetation. But today we understand the statement that the earth has been made a cradle for you with somewhat greater breadth and depth, to the extent that we have acquired information about this earth, and have gathered information about its distant and near history, provided that the theories which are formed about our own sciences are correct and the estimates and approximations that we make prove accurate. The generations that come after us will understand about them even more than we do. Thus the meaning of this verse will keep expanding. As we advance in knowledge, the meanings of this verse will also widen along with the conquests of knowledge and recognition, and thus the veil of human ignorance will keep receding.

Today we know how well this earth has been made as a cradle for man, and how many different paths of life man is seeking within it. The truth is that this globe passed through various stages to reach its present state, and was made a cradle for man. Among these stages, one stage was that the entire surface of this earth was a hard rock. After that, soil was deposited in various places, and plants began to grow in it, and from the combination of hydrogen gas and oxygen gas present on its surface, water came into being. Then, as a result of its rotation on its axis, such moderate heat arose during its day that it became suitable for the life of animals. And the speed of its axial rotation was kept such that it became possible for things to remain standing on its surface, and houses and other things did not scatter and fly off into the air.

Then Allah created gravitational force in this earth. Thus a layer of air came into being in which life became possible. If the air surrounding this earth were to escape the earth's attraction, nothing on earth could remain alive. And since the surfaces of other celestial bodies have no attraction, or a weaker one, life has not been possible there. Air has gone from those spheres. For instance, there is no air above the moon. This attraction is so balanced that it creates the balance in the effect of throwing things away produced by the motion of the earth. Thus all things and living beings are safe from the process of scattering and flying away, and here on the surface of the earth their standing and walking is entirely possible. If this attraction were to increase beyond its present measure, all living and dead things would be flattened against the earth, and it would become impossible, or very difficult, for humans to take a step, and a great deal of force would have to be expended for it. And if the pressure of air upon humans from the other side were to increase, it would press humans flat against the earth, just as we kill mosquitoes and flies by concentrating pressure on them without touching them. And if this pressure were to decrease below what it is, our chests and our arteries would burst from the pressure of the blood.

And regarding making the earth a cradle and making its paths level upon it, we know that Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, has placed within this earth harmonious forces which, all together, make life on this earth easy. If even one of these harmonious or life-supporting forces were to vanish, or be disturbed, life on this globe would become impossible. Some of them we have mentioned above, and others exist. For instance, Allah has kept the quantity of waters on this earth such that the seas and rivers, in the form of waters, absorb all the poisonous gases which arise on the surface of the earth, and keep the atmosphere of the earth so clean from pollution that the existence of life becomes possible here. Then Allah made vegetation the means of maintaining balance between oxygen: the oxygen which man takes in through breath, and the oxygen which plants release. If this balance did not exist, after a period man would die of suffocation.

These and other such meanings are included in this verse.

﴿He who made for you the earth a cradle and made for you therein roads.﴾ (43:10). Every moment and every day, new meanings are being unveiled, and these meanings and implications are added to the meanings which the first addressees of this verse understood. And all of these show the knowledge of Allah, the Ruler of the heavens and the earth, and they are also manifestations of His power, which is Almighty and full of wisdom. All these meanings show a heart possessing awareness that there is a Creator and a Governing Power. As a person's vision advances and his thought reaches to depth, he understands that he is not a creature left to wander aimlessly, and that he will not be left unaccountable, but rather a person becomes certain that a Governor of mighty power has laid hold of them and that He is the guardian of all their affairs, in life and after life.

﴿That you may be guided.﴾ (43:10). Such deep reflection upon this universe, and the study of the laws of nature present within it, guarantees that the human heart and mind turn toward the Creator of the universe, who has placed such profound order and balance within it.

After the growth of life, the provisions for the living, the making of the earth a cradle, and the making of paths for humans upon it, now one step further:

﴿And He who sent down water from the sky in a measure, and We revived thereby a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ (43:11). The water that is sent down from the heavens is seen and known by every human being, but most people see this scene and pass it by without any wonder, and no tremor arises in their awareness and consciousness. Why? Because they have constantly seen the descent of the rain of mercy, and at times. But the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) used to look at the drops of rain with great love, great interest and great joy, because he had firm awareness that they were coming from Allah, since his living and awakened heart clearly saw that these drops are supreme examples of Allah's attributes. He was seeing in them the craftsmanship of the hand of power. Upon these drops, a heart which has reached Allah and knows the laws of nature which Allah has set in motion in this universe should look in the same way. For these raindrops are the results of those laws of nature. These laws of nature, under Allah's watch in this universe and through the hand of Allah's power, fall drop by drop. The necessity of this truth and its effects cannot be diminished by the thought that this water was in fact vapour which rose from the earth into the atmosphere, cooled, and in the skies became so dense that it rained. The question is: who created the earth? Who made water here? Then who imposed heat upon them, and who fashioned the nature of the substance so that it turns into vapour from heat? Then who placed in vapours the property that they rise? And then become dense again above? Then who placed these properties? These vapours are also filled with electricity, which when they meet, the water falls down. And what is electricity? In short, what are all those natural properties from which rain is formed?

By reading science, in truth, we make the veils of our feeling so dense that the wonders of this universe have no effect upon us, whereas what we ought to do is to sharpen our feelings through science, so sharp that hearts tremble with the fear of God.

﴿And He who sent down water from the sky in a measure.﴾ (43:11). This water is ordained and suitable within a measure: it is not so much that it drowns people, nor so little that the earth dries up and ceases to be fit for life. We see this wondrous balance and measure, and today we know well that this balance is necessary for the requirements of life, and that it was established by the will of Allah.

﴿And We revived thereby a dead land.﴾ (43:11). Revival means ihya (giving life), and every kind of life comes after water, because Allah made every thing alive through water.

﴿Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ (43:11). He who first gave life can give life again. He who brought living things out of dead earth for the first time will, in the same way, bring all living humans out on the Day of Resurrection in the place of gathering. When the beginning has occurred, repetition and recurrence are no longer difficult. There is no difficulty for Allah in this.

Then, these cattle which these people divide, giving some to Allah and some to others as partners besides Allah: Allah did not create them so that you should divide them in this manner. They have been created so that they serve as a blessing of Allah for people. People ride upon them just as they ride upon ships, and give thanks to Allah for this subjugation of them. And they should give thanks in return for Allah's bounties.

﴿And He who created all the pairs, and made for you ships and cattle to ride upon, so that you may sit firmly upon their backs, and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are seated upon them, and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, though we were not capable of controlling them. ﴿And made for you ships and cattle to ride upon.﴾ (43:12). Here the reference is to this: that He made you the vicegerent of Allah on earth, and subjected to you all the forces and powers of this earth. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 43, verses 10–14 (part 2 of 2):

﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs; and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are seated upon them, and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, though we could not have subdued them ourselves. And to our Lord indeed we shall return."﴾ (43:13–14)

Then let them remember that, after fulfilling their responsibility of vicegerency (khilafah) on the earth, they will return to Allah, and He will reward them for all the deeds they performed in fulfilling the duty of khilafah. Here He has bestowed favours upon them and subjected the whole world to them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 10–14 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 9 to 14

The Arabs believed in God, and they followed the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham). However, what remained among the Arabs was a distorted form of the millat-e-Ibrahimi (the religion of Abraham). Many changes had taken place in it. In place of tawhid (the oneness of God), shirk and other fables had entered it. Nonetheless, they acknowledged the existence of the Creator, because human nature cannot in any case deny that there is a Creator, who is Allah. For no sound-natured person can deny a Creator. And no reasonable person can say that this great and awe-inspiring universe came into being without a Creator. Nor can anyone other than Allah create this universe, because the Creator of this great universe must be even greater and more powerful than it. But they would stop at this point and would not accept the necessary demands of their own belief.

﴿And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ (43:9). It is clear that these two attributes, the Almighty and the All-Knowing, were not the statement of the disbelievers. They only acknowledged that He is Allah; they did not accept the attributes which Islam and the Quran presented, attributes which have a positive effect on their lives, and which govern their lives and this universe simultaneously in practice. They acknowledged Allah merely as the Creator of this universe, and they also acknowledged Allah as their own Creator. But for running life in practice, they had made other beings. This was because they were not acquainted with such attributes of Allah, after which they would have no need of shirk, and the doctrine of shirk would appear to them as hollow and worthless.

The Quran here teaches them this very thing: that the God whom you consider the Creator of the heavens and the earth is also the Almighty and the All-Knowing. He is also All-Powerful, and He is also All-Knowing and All-Aware. Therefore Allah, taking their acknowledgement as a foundation, compels them to the following acknowledgements. In short, He takes them one step further and tells them that after creation, Allah has bestowed this favour upon you:

﴿He it is who made the earth a cradle for you and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided.﴾ (43:10). The fact that Allah made the earth a cradle for man has been understood and depicted by every age of humanity according to the limits of its knowledge. Those who heard this for the first time must also have understood that Allah made the earth suitable so that it is fit for walking upon with their feet. Then it is suitable for agriculture. Then it is suitable for life and vegetation. But today we understand the statement that the earth has been made a cradle for you with somewhat greater breadth and depth, to the extent that we have acquired information about this earth, and have gathered information about its distant and near history, provided that the theories which are formed about our own sciences are correct and the estimates and approximations that we make prove accurate. The generations that come after us will understand about them even more than we do. Thus the meaning of this verse will keep expanding. As we advance in knowledge, the meanings of this verse will also widen along with the conquests of knowledge and recognition, and thus the veil of human ignorance will keep receding.

Today we know how well this earth has been made as a cradle for man, and how many different paths of life man is seeking within it. The truth is that this globe passed through various stages to reach its present state, and was made a cradle for man. Among these stages, one stage was that the entire surface of this earth was a hard rock. After that, soil was deposited in various places, and plants began to grow in it, and from the combination of hydrogen gas and oxygen gas present on its surface, water came into being. Then, as a result of its rotation on its axis, such moderate heat arose during its day that it became suitable for the life of animals. And the speed of its axial rotation was kept such that it became possible for things to remain standing on its surface, and houses and other things did not scatter and fly off into the air.

Then Allah created gravitational force in this earth. Thus a layer of air came into being in which life became possible. If the air surrounding this earth were to escape the earth's attraction, nothing on earth could remain alive. And since the surfaces of other celestial bodies have no attraction, or a weaker one, life has not been possible there. Air has gone from those spheres. For instance, there is no air above the moon. This attraction is so balanced that it creates the balance in the effect of throwing things away produced by the motion of the earth. Thus all things and living beings are safe from the process of scattering and flying away, and here on the surface of the earth their standing and walking is entirely possible. If this attraction were to increase beyond its present measure, all living and dead things would be flattened against the earth, and it would become impossible, or very difficult, for humans to take a step, and a great deal of force would have to be expended for it. And if the pressure of air upon humans from the other side were to increase, it would press humans flat against the earth, just as we kill mosquitoes and flies by concentrating pressure on them without touching them. And if this pressure were to decrease below what it is, our chests and our arteries would burst from the pressure of the blood.

And regarding making the earth a cradle and making its paths level upon it, we know that Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, has placed within this earth harmonious forces which, all together, make life on this earth easy. If even one of these harmonious or life-supporting forces were to vanish, or be disturbed, life on this globe would become impossible. Some of them we have mentioned above, and others exist. For instance, Allah has kept the quantity of waters on this earth such that the seas and rivers, in the form of waters, absorb all the poisonous gases which arise on the surface of the earth, and keep the atmosphere of the earth so clean from pollution that the existence of life becomes possible here. Then Allah made vegetation the means of maintaining balance between oxygen: the oxygen which man takes in through breath, and the oxygen which plants release. If this balance did not exist, after a period man would die of suffocation.

These and other such meanings are included in this verse.

﴿He who made for you the earth a cradle and made for you therein roads.﴾ (43:10). Every moment and every day, new meanings are being unveiled, and these meanings and implications are added to the meanings which the first addressees of this verse understood. And all of these show the knowledge of Allah, the Ruler of the heavens and the earth, and they are also manifestations of His power, which is Almighty and full of wisdom. All these meanings show a heart possessing awareness that there is a Creator and a Governing Power. As a person's vision advances and his thought reaches to depth, he understands that he is not a creature left to wander aimlessly, and that he will not be left unaccountable, but rather a person becomes certain that a Governor of mighty power has laid hold of them and that He is the guardian of all their affairs, in life and after life.

﴿That you may be guided.﴾ (43:10). Such deep reflection upon this universe, and the study of the laws of nature present within it, guarantees that the human heart and mind turn toward the Creator of the universe, who has placed such profound order and balance within it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 10–14 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 9 to 14

The Arabs believed in God, and they followed the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham). However, what remained among the Arabs was a distorted form of the millat-e-Ibrahimi (the religion of Abraham). Many changes had taken place in it. In place of tawhid (the oneness of God), shirk and other fables had entered it. Nonetheless, they acknowledged the existence of the Creator, because human nature cannot in any case deny that there is a Creator, who is Allah. For no sound-natured person can deny a Creator. And no reasonable person can say that this great and awe-inspiring universe came into being without a Creator. Nor can anyone other than Allah create this universe, because the Creator of this great universe must be even greater and more powerful than it. But they would stop at this point and would not accept the necessary demands of their own belief.

﴿And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ (43:9). It is clear that these two attributes, the Almighty and the All-Knowing, were not the statement of the disbelievers. They only acknowledged that He is Allah; they did not accept the attributes which Islam and the Quran presented, attributes which have a positive effect on their lives, and which govern their lives and this universe simultaneously in practice. They acknowledged Allah merely as the Creator of this universe, and they also acknowledged Allah as their own Creator. But for running life in practice, they had made other beings. This was because they were not acquainted with such attributes of Allah, after which they would have no need of shirk, and the doctrine of shirk would appear to them as hollow and worthless.

The Quran here teaches them this very thing: that the God whom you consider the Creator of the heavens and the earth is also the Almighty and the All-Knowing. He is also All-Powerful, and He is also All-Knowing and All-Aware. Therefore Allah, taking their acknowledgement as a foundation, compels them to the following acknowledgements. In short, He takes them one step further and tells them that after creation, Allah has bestowed this favour upon you:

﴿He it is who made the earth a cradle for you and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided.﴾ (43:10). The fact that Allah made the earth a cradle for man has been understood and depicted by every age of humanity according to the limits of its knowledge. Those who heard this for the first time must also have understood that Allah made the earth suitable so that it is fit for walking upon with their feet. Then it is suitable for agriculture. Then it is suitable for life and vegetation. But today we understand the statement that the earth has been made a cradle for you with somewhat greater breadth and depth, to the extent that we have acquired information about this earth, and have gathered information about its distant and near history, provided that the theories which are formed about our own sciences are correct and the estimates and approximations that we make prove accurate. The generations that come after us will understand about them even more than we do. Thus the meaning of this verse will keep expanding. As we advance in knowledge, the meanings of this verse will also widen along with the conquests of knowledge and recognition, and thus the veil of human ignorance will keep receding.

Today we know how well this earth has been made as a cradle for man, and how many different paths of life man is seeking within it. The truth is that this globe passed through various stages to reach its present state, and was made a cradle for man. Among these stages, one stage was that the entire surface of this earth was a hard rock. After that, soil was deposited in various places, and plants began to grow in it, and from the combination of hydrogen gas and oxygen gas present on its surface, water came into being. Then, as a result of its rotation on its axis, such moderate heat arose during its day that it became suitable for the life of animals. And the speed of its axial rotation was kept such that it became possible for things to remain standing on its surface, and houses and other things did not scatter and fly off into the air.

Then Allah created gravitational force in this earth. Thus a layer of air came into being in which life became possible. If the air surrounding this earth were to escape the earth's attraction, nothing on earth could remain alive. And since the surfaces of other celestial bodies have no attraction, or a weaker one, life has not been possible there. Air has gone from those spheres. For instance, there is no air above the moon. This attraction is so balanced that it creates the balance in the effect of throwing things away produced by the motion of the earth. Thus all things and living beings are safe from the process of scattering and flying away, and here on the surface of the earth their standing and walking is entirely possible. If this attraction were to increase beyond its present measure, all living and dead things would be flattened against the earth, and it would become impossible, or very difficult, for humans to take a step, and a great deal of force would have to be expended for it. And if the pressure of air upon humans from the other side were to increase, it would press humans flat against the earth, just as we kill mosquitoes and flies by concentrating pressure on them without touching them. And if this pressure were to decrease below what it is, our chests and our arteries would burst from the pressure of the blood.

And regarding making the earth a cradle and making its paths level upon it, we know that Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, has placed within this earth harmonious forces which, all together, make life on this earth easy. If even one of these harmonious or life-supporting forces were to vanish, or be disturbed, life on this globe would become impossible. Some of them we have mentioned above, and others exist. For instance, Allah has kept the quantity of waters on this earth such that the seas and rivers, in the form of waters, absorb all the poisonous gases which arise on the surface of the earth, and keep the atmosphere of the earth so clean from pollution that the existence of life becomes possible here. Then Allah made vegetation the means of maintaining balance between oxygen: the oxygen which man takes in through breath, and the oxygen which plants release. If this balance did not exist, after a period man would die of suffocation.

These and other such meanings are included in this verse.

﴿He who made for you the earth a cradle and made for you therein roads.﴾ (43:10). Every moment and every day, new meanings are being unveiled, and these meanings and implications are added to the meanings which the first addressees of this verse understood. And all of these show the knowledge of Allah, the Ruler of the heavens and the earth, and they are also manifestations of His power, which is Almighty and full of wisdom. All these meanings show a heart possessing awareness that there is a Creator and a Governing Power. As a person's vision advances and his thought reaches to depth, he understands that he is not a creature left to wander aimlessly, and that he will not be left unaccountable, but rather a person becomes certain that a Governor of mighty power has laid hold of them and that He is the guardian of all their affairs, in life and after life.

﴿That you may be guided.﴾ (43:10). Such deep reflection upon this universe, and the study of the laws of nature present within it, guarantees that the human heart and mind turn toward the Creator of the universe, who has placed such profound order and balance within it.

After the growth of life, the provisions for the living, the making of the earth a cradle, and the making of paths for humans upon it, now one step further:

﴿And He who sent down water from the sky in a measure, and We revived thereby a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ (43:11). The water that is sent down from the heavens is seen and known by every human being, but most people see this scene and pass it by without any wonder, and no tremor arises in their awareness and consciousness. Why? Because they have constantly seen the descent of the rain of mercy, and at times. But the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) used to look at the drops of rain with great love, great interest and great joy, because he had firm awareness that they were coming from Allah, since his living and awakened heart clearly saw that these drops are supreme examples of Allah's attributes. He was seeing in them the craftsmanship of the hand of power. Upon these drops, a heart which has reached Allah and knows the laws of nature which Allah has set in motion in this universe should look in the same way. For these raindrops are the results of those laws of nature. These laws of nature, under Allah's watch in this universe and through the hand of Allah's power, fall drop by drop. The necessity of this truth and its effects cannot be diminished by the thought that this water was in fact vapour which rose from the earth into the atmosphere, cooled, and in the skies became so dense that it rained. The question is: who created the earth? Who made water here? Then who imposed heat upon them, and who fashioned the nature of the substance so that it turns into vapour from heat? Then who placed in vapours the property that they rise? And then become dense again above? Then who placed these properties? These vapours are also filled with electricity, which when they meet, the water falls down. And what is electricity? In short, what are all those natural properties from which rain is formed?

By reading science, in truth, we make the veils of our feeling so dense that the wonders of this universe have no effect upon us, whereas what we ought to do is to sharpen our feelings through science, so sharp that hearts tremble with the fear of God.

﴿And He who sent down water from the sky in a measure.﴾ (43:11). This water is ordained and suitable within a measure: it is not so much that it drowns people, nor so little that the earth dries up and ceases to be fit for life. We see this wondrous balance and measure, and today we know well that this balance is necessary for the requirements of life, and that it was established by the will of Allah.

﴿And We revived thereby a dead land.﴾ (43:11). Revival means ihya (giving life), and every kind of life comes after water, because Allah made every thing alive through water.

﴿Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ (43:11). He who first gave life can give life again. He who brought living things out of dead earth for the first time will, in the same way, bring all living humans out on the Day of Resurrection in the place of gathering. When the beginning has occurred, repetition and recurrence are no longer difficult. There is no difficulty for Allah in this.

Then, these cattle which these people divide, giving some to Allah and some to others as partners besides Allah: Allah did not create them so that you should divide them in this manner. They have been created so that they serve as a blessing of Allah for people. People ride upon them just as they ride upon ships, and give thanks to Allah for this subjugation of them. And they should give thanks in return for Allah's bounties.

﴿And He who created all the pairs, and made for you ships and cattle to ride upon, so that you may sit firmly upon their backs, and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are seated upon them, and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, though we were not capable of controlling them. And to our Lord we are surely returning."﴾ (43:12–14).

Allah has based the continuity of life upon the principle of pairing. All living things are in pairs. Even the first cell carries within it the characteristics of masculinity and femininity. Indeed, scientific research has shown that the whole universe depends upon pairs; and if we accept that the first unit of the universe is the atom, composed of the negative electron and the positive proton, then this too is a pair, and physical research continues along this same path.

In any case, the system of pairing in life is entirely evident, and it is Allah who created all the pairs, whether among humans or among animals.

﴿And made for you ships and cattle to ride upon.﴾ (43:12). Here the reference is to this: that He made you the vicegerent of Allah on earth, and subjected to you all the forces and powers of this earth. After this He draws their attention to the fact that gratitude for these blessings is obligatory, and that the etiquette of this station must be observed. And whenever a blessing appears before you, remember the Bestower, so that hearts remain connected to the Creator, in every movement and every stillness of life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 15–25:

Verses 15 to 25

The Quran attacks this mythical belief in such a way that it is surrounded from every side and confronted within their own world from every direction, until every path by which it could reach their minds is closed. Then the Quranic reasoning is based on their own logic and their own accepted premises, and these arguments rest upon the events of their own lives. Moreover, the Quran also presents before them the example of earlier nations: whoever adopted this belief, We took from them a retribution that serves as a lesson.

The discussion begins with the weakness of this belief, and with the fact that in the sight of God it is a great sin and clear disbelief.

﴿And they have made of His servants a part of Him. Indeed, man is a manifest ingrate.﴾ (43:15) The angels are God's servants, and to call them God's daughters means that they have been deprived of the quality of servanthood to God and given the station of close kinship with God, although they, like all creatures, are created and are servants of God. There is no argument by which we may attribute to them any quality other than servanthood to God, or define for them any relationship with their Lord other than that. Since all of God's creation, male and female, are His servants, whoever makes claims of this kind commits clear disbelief.

﴿Indeed, man is a manifest ingrate.﴾ (43:15)

After this, they are refuted by their own customs and their own mentality, and thus it is shown how false their claim is and how insulting it is to God that you call the angels God's daughters.

﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ (43:16) If God was going to have offspring, how is it that He Himself produced daughters and favoured you with sons? And is it fitting for them to say such a thing, when they themselves become deeply displeased when a daughter is born to them?

﴿And when one of them is given the news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark and he is filled with suppressed grief.﴾ (43:17) Did propriety, respect and humanity not require that they should not attribute to the Most Merciful the offspring at whose birth they themselves are displeased? They themselves are so angered at the birth of daughters that their faces turn black, they do not show themselves to anyone, they hide the news of the birth, and they come close to dying of that grief. Do they attribute to God that weak creature which is raised among ornaments, lives in great pampering and delicacy, and cannot even express its own view, nor take part in war and fighting, while for themselves they desire offspring that is sharp and agile and, at the time of battle, a horseman?

﴿And when one of them is given the news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark and he is filled with suppressed grief.﴾ (43:17) Did propriety, respect and humanity not require that they should not attribute to the Most Merciful the offspring at whose birth they themselves are displeased? They themselves are so angered at the birth of daughters that their faces turn black, they do not show themselves to anyone, they hide the news of the birth, and they come close to dying of that grief. Do they attribute to God that weak creature which is raised among ornaments, lives in great pampering and delicacy, and cannot even express its own view, nor take part in war and fighting, while for themselves they desire offspring that is sharp and agile and, at the time of battle, a horseman?

In short, the Quran here reasons with regard to their psychology and shames them: the offspring you do not like for yourselves, you like for God. If you were going to commit this folly, you should have made for God an attribution that you yourselves would also like for yourselves, if this disbelief was to be committed by you. Now their mythical belief is to be confronted from another angle. Their claim is that the angels are daughters. On what basis do they make this claim?

﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.﴾ (43:19) When the angels were being created, were these people present there, so that they can say that they are daughters? For whoever makes a claim must have eyewitness testimony that proves his claim. They did not claim, nor could they claim, that they had seen the physical form of the angels. Yet, despite not having seen this form, they still make this claim and give this testimony. Therefore, let them now be prepared to bear the consequences of this false testimony.

﴿Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.﴾ (43:19)

After this, their fabrication is discussed further, and the false arguments they brought in its support are refuted.

This is in fact a deception. It is true that everything in this universe happens by the will of God, but within the scope of the will of God is also that man may take guidance or may take the path of misguidance, and God has made it an obligation upon man that he adopt guidance, and God is pleased with that. And if man is misguided and a disbeliever, God is displeased, even though the will of God has made him capable of both guidance and misguidance.

﴿They have no knowledge of that; they are only guessing.﴾ (43:20) They have no knowledge of this matter; they only throw random guesses and believe in illusions and superstitions.

﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ (43:21) Their claim is not based on the texts of any book, and they have not derived this worship from any book, nor do they possess its proofs. Thus the path of transmitted proof is also closed to these people, and it is shown that beliefs and doctrines are not established by idle talk or by shooting arrows in the dark, nor are beliefs established by mere conjecture and estimation. Beliefs are clearly established by the Books of God.

Finally, it is shown that their only proof for this mythical belief, which is based neither on eyewitness testimony nor derived from any book, is merely this:

﴿Rather, they say, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are, upon their footsteps, guided."﴾ (43:22) This is a most ridiculous argument. Moreover, in terms of evidence it is also a base matter. It is mere imitation and blind following, and they have not reflected upon it, nor examined it through sound reasoning and logical method. Their example is like a herd which the driver leads wherever he wishes. No one asks why they are being driven in this direction, where they are going, or why they are going.

Islam is also a message of thought and freedom, and a movement for freedom of conscience and belief. Islam does not accept this kind of rigid imitation. It does not tolerate sin and misguidance merely because our forefathers did so. Every act, every claim, and every statement requires proof. Before every undertaking there is need for reflection. After that, it grants man a self-determination based on knowledge and certainty.

Finally, it is shown what was the end, in history, of those who adopted such mythical beliefs and took the path of mere imitation and rigid following, to whom the truth was made clear, and from whom the excuse was removed that the correct message had not reached them, and who nevertheless turned away from accepting the truth.

﴿And similarly, We did not send before you any warner into a city but that its affluent said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are, upon their footsteps, following."﴾ (43:23) ﴿He said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that upon which you found your fathers?" They said, "Indeed, we are, in what you have been sent with, disbelievers."﴾ (43:24) ﴿So We took retribution from them, and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ (43:25)

It appears that the reasoning and temperament of all who turn away are one and the same: "We found our fathers upon this way, and we follow in their footsteps." Simply imitation, with eyes closed, and the intellect blinded. Those who imitate without reflection, even if what is presented to them is more reasonable than their imitated beliefs and practices, and even if it is backed by a mountain of arguments and evidence, such people of this nature are better off destroyed, for they do not open their eyes to see, nor open their hearts to understand, nor open their minds to weigh arguments.

This is the end of people of this kind, and it is presented before them so that they may understand, beware, and be warned of the outcome of this path.

Lesson No. 232: At a Glance

The Quraysh claimed that they were descendants of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). This claim was true. But they also claimed that they followed the millah (religious path) of Ibrahim, and this claim was false. Ibrahim had announced the belief in tawhid (the oneness of Allah) with great clarity, without any ambiguity or complexity. For this reason he left his father and left his people, and before that an attempt had been made to kill him and to burn him. His shari'ah (law) also rested upon the belief in tawhid, and it was this that he enjoined upon his offspring. Therefore, in the da'wah (call) and shari'ah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) there was not even a trace of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

In this lesson the Qur'an takes its addressees on a tour of their own history, so that their claim may be tested against the touchstone of history. After this, their objections to the prophethood of Muhammad are being examined.

﴿وَقَالُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾ (43:31) "They say: Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon some great man of the two cities?" Their statement is refuted, showing that there is a very great crookedness in their thinking. For according to the values on which Islam is based, this very thinking is wrong, the idea that the reins of the Islamic call are held by some great man. These are false values, and it is these that stand as an obstacle for them in coming to Islam. It is these false thoughts that have kept them far from truth and guidance. After this judgment, they are also informed that the real cause and reason for this misguidance is that Satan whispers waswasah (evil suggestions) into their hearts. At the end of this lesson, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is directed to turn away from them, to leave them to their condition; you do not have the power to make a blind man see or to give hearing to a deaf man. They have become blind and deaf. And they will surely be punished, whether Allah takes revenge upon them during your lifetime or they encounter it after you. You are instructed to hold firmly to the message given to you, for this same message was given to all the prophets; all of them brought the kalimah of tawhid.

﴿وَاسْأَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَا ۖ أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾ (43:45) "Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?" After this, a segment of the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) is presented: that part of the account of Pharaoh, in which those same false values come forward which the people of Makkah presented concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is, as it were, a ready-made argument, already formed, and it is repeated at every stage of history.

Lesson No. 232: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 26 to 56

Verses 26 to 28: The call to tawhid, which these people regard as strange, is in fact the call of their own forefather. It is the call that he presented before his father and his people, refuting their false beliefs. In it he abandoned the inherited beliefs of his forefathers and did not walk the hereditary path merely because their forefathers had been doing so. In declaring his disavowal of them, Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not speak with any ambiguity, but refuted them in the clearest words and the most transparent conduct, as the Qur'an relates:

﴿إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ * إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ﴾ (43:26-27) "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for He will surely guide me."

From Ibrahim's declaration of disavowal, and then his announcement that he would worship only the God who is his Creator, it becomes apparent that the Nimrodian society was not entirely denying God, but rather they associated other deities with Allah and worshipped them. Therefore he declared his disavowal of them. In this statement of disassociation, he excepted the Creator of the universe, and by mentioning this attribute of Allah he established that Allah alone deserves worship: that He is the Creator. Therefore worship and command too must belong to Him. He also expressed his certainty that Allah would give them guidance as to what they should do, for the Creator also makes arrangements for the guidance of His creation, and Allah knows best how to guide. This kalimah, upon which life is founded, upon which this whole universe is founded, and to which it bears witness, is what Ibrahim spoke.

﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ (43:28) "And he made it a lasting word among his posterity, that they might return." A large part of Prophet Ibrahim's call lies in the affirmation and spread of the kalimah of tawhid upon this earth. After him, this kalimah became prevalent among all generations, and this spread came through his offspring. From his descendants countless prophets were sent. Three of them were ulul-azm (messengers of firm resolve): Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ. Today in the world there are more than one billion people who are followers of various major religions and who adhere to the tawhid of their forefather. He preserved this kalimah among his offspring. Although among them too, those who went astray did go astray, yet this kalimah remained. It never became entirely extinct, its foundations stayed firm, no one ever uprooted it completely, and it has not been mingled with falsehood, so that people may return to Allah and embrace it.

Before Ibrahim (peace be upon him), humanity was already acquainted with the kalimah of tawhid, but the establishment and stability of the kalimah of tawhid upon the earth was granted after Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Before him, Nuh, Hud, Salih and perhaps Idris (peace be upon them) presented the kalimah of tawhid, but these messengers did not find successors who would preserve the kalimah of tawhid after them, live according to it, and live for it. But when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) presented this kalimah, its continuity was established after him, and an unbroken chain of messengers came into being. Thus, from among his offspring came the last son, and the one most resembling him, Muhammad, Seal of the Prophets ﷺ, and he presented the kalimah of tawhid in its complete and comprehensive form, which encompassed the entire life around this kalimah and affected every activity of human beings.

This was the story of tawhid, from Ibrahim (peace be upon him) onward. Those whom the people of Quraysh claimed were upon the religion of Ibrahim, and that kalimah which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) preserved as an inheritance among his offspring, and from Ibrahim (peace be upon him) onward this kalimah was transmitted generation after generation. Now the question is what reaction those who ascribe themselves to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) adopt towards this kalimah.

Ages passed. Allah gave them, generation after generation, abundant provisions of life, and after going very far away, they forgot the millah of Ibrahim. And among these Arabs the kalimah of tawhid became strange. Now when Muhammad ﷺ came, they received him very badly, and began to measure him too by the standards of the people of the earth and worldly-minded people, and their own standards too changed.

﴿وَقَالُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾ (43:31) "They say: Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon some great man of the two cities?" Their statement is refuted, showing that there is a very great crookedness in their thinking. For according to the values on which Islam is based, this very thinking is wrong, the idea that the reins of the Islamic call are held by some great man. These are false values, and it is these that stand as an obstacle for them in coming to Islam. It is these false thoughts that have kept them far from truth and guidance. After this judgment, they are also informed that the real cause and reason for this misguidance is that Satan whispers waswasah (evil suggestions) into their hearts. At the end of this lesson, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is directed to turn away from them, to leave them to their condition; you do not have the power to make a blind man see or to give hearing to a deaf man. They have become blind and deaf. And they will surely be punished, whether Allah takes revenge upon them during your lifetime or they encounter it after you. You are instructed to hold firmly to the message given to you, for this same message was given to all the prophets; all of them brought the kalimah of tawhid.

﴿وَاسْأَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَا ۖ أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾ (43:45) "Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?" After this, a segment of the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) is presented: that part of the account of Pharaoh, in which those same false values come forward which the people of Makkah presented concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is, as it were, a ready-made argument, already formed, and it is repeated at every stage of history.

Lesson No. 232: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 26 to 56

Verses 26 to 28: The call to tawhid, which these people regard as strange, is in fact the call of their own forefather. It is the call that he presented before his father and his people, refuting their false beliefs. In it he abandoned the inherited beliefs of his forefathers and did not walk the hereditary path merely because their forefathers had been doing so. In declaring his disavowal of them, Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not speak with any ambiguity, but refuted them in the clearest words and the most transparent conduct, as the Qur'an relates:

﴿إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ * إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ﴾ (43:26-27) "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me, for He will surely guide me."

From Ibrahim's declaration of disavowal, and then his announcement that he would worship only the God who is his Creator, it becomes apparent that the Nimrodian society was not entirely denying God, but rather they associated other deities with Allah and worshipped them. Therefore he declared his disavowal of them. In this statement of disassociation, he excepted the Creator of the universe, and by mentioning this attribute of Allah he established that Allah alone deserves worship: that He is the Creator. Therefore worship and command too must belong to Him. He also expressed his certainty that Allah would give them guidance as to what they should do, for the Creator also makes arrangements for the guidance of His creation, and Allah knows best how to guide. This kalimah, upon which life is founded, upon which this whole universe is founded, and to which it bears witness, is what Ibrahim spoke.

﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ (43:28) "And he made it a lasting word among his posterity, that they might return." A large part of Prophet Ibrahim's call lies in the affirmation and spread of the kalimah of tawhid upon this earth. After him, this kalimah became prevalent among all generations, and this spread came through his offspring. From his descendants countless prophets were sent. Three of them were ulul-azm (messengers of firm resolve): Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ. Today in the world there are more than one billion people who are followers of various major religions and who adhere to the tawhid of their forefather. He preserved this kalimah among his offspring. Although among them too, those who went astray did go astray, yet this kalimah remained. It never became entirely extinct, its foundations stayed firm, no one ever uprooted it completely, and it has not been mingled with falsehood, so that people may return to Allah and embrace it.

Before Ibrahim (peace be upon him), humanity was already acquainted with the kalimah of tawhid, but the establishment and stability of the kalimah of tawhid upon the earth was granted after Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Before him, Nuh, Hud, Salih and perhaps Idris (peace be upon them) presented the kalimah of tawhid, but these messengers did not find successors who would preserve the kalimah of tawhid after them, live according to it, and live for it. But when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) presented this kalimah, its continuity was established after him, and an unbroken chain of messengers came into being. Thus, from among his offspring came the last son, and the one most resembling him, Muhammad, Seal of the Prophets ﷺ, and he presented the kalimah of tawhid in its complete and comprehensive form, which encompassed the entire life around this kalimah and affected every activity of human beings.

This was the story of tawhid, from Ibrahim (peace be upon him) onward. Those whom the people of Quraysh claimed were upon the religion of Ibrahim, and that kalimah which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) preserved as an inheritance among his offspring, and from Ibrahim (peace be upon him) onward this kalimah was transmitted generation after generation. Now the question is what reaction those who ascribe themselves to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) adopt towards this kalimah.

Ages passed. Allah gave them, generation after generation, abundant provisions of life, and after going very far away, they forgot the millah of Ibrahim. And among these Arabs the kalimah of tawhid became strange. Now when Muhammad ﷺ came, they received him very badly, and began to measure him too by the standards of the people of the earth and worldly-minded people, and their own standards too changed.
