Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 29–35 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 29 to 35

Now the direction of address in the context suddenly turns back to the people of Makkah. This is called iḍrāb (a shift of direction in speech), and this style was current among the Arabs.

﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a plainly-spoken Messenger﴾ (43:29). That is, "Leave aside the matter of Ibrahim (peace be upon him); what connection and relationship do these people have with it? We should look at their way of life, and their conditions do not match those of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Their condition is that they and their forefathers were given abundant provision of life and were granted a long respite, until the truth came to them in the form of this Qur'an, and with it a Messenger who explains matters most clearly came to them, who presents this truth to them and presents it with great clarity."

﴿But when the truth came to them, they said, "This is sorcery, and we disbelieve in it"﴾ (43:30). Although the reality is that sorcery does not have even a trace of truth in it, and this is quite clear. This was merely their claim and accusation, and the first to be convinced that this accusation was false were the leaders of Quraysh themselves, because the great men of Quraysh were so experienced that it could not have remained hidden from them that the Qur'an is the word of truth. They made these accusations only to deceive the common masses. Thus they say that it is sorcery, and then they declare that they disbelieve in it. They made this declaration in order to make the claim firm.

﴿And we disbelieve in it﴾ (43:30). Through this, they gave the common people the impression that they were fully certain of what they were saying. In this way they gave them the signal: keep following us and remain obedient to us. The chiefs of every people deceive the common masses in this way, lest they step outside their sphere of authority and accept the word of Tawhid. For when the authority of the word of Tawhid is established, all tyrants are brought down. Then only the worship of Allah remains, and people fear Allah alone.

After this, the Qur'an shows how they have mixed the sound and the unsound values together. They object that Allah chose Muhammad ﷺ to convey this message.

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?"﴾ (43:31). By "the two cities" they mean Makkah and Ta'if. The Messenger ﷺ was from a branch of Quraysh, then a member of a branch of Banu Hashim, and these people were among the noblest of the Arabs, while his own person was also distinguished in lofty morals. Before prophethood he was known as a truthful and trustworthy man of excellent character. But he was not the chief of his tribe, nor the leader of any clan, and in that age people took pride in exactly these things: that someone should be the head of a tribe or a branch. This was the basis of the objection of the objectors.

﴿They say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?"﴾ (43:31). Yet Allah alone knows who is suitable for His message and His call, and to whom this office should be given. Therefore, Allah chose the most worthy person. It was not Allah's purpose that this message should receive support from external causes; its strength should not come from outside it, but from within. Therefore He chose for it a personality whose principal quality was his character. This is the very nature of this call, and it is its distinctive feature. For this reason, the chief of a tribe was not chosen, nor the head of a family, nor a person of rank and influence, nor a very wealthy man, so that the real values of this call, which descended from the heavens, would not become mixed with any value connected with worldliness, and so that no element of worldliness would enter this call, having no connection with its reality. And so that no external cause other than the inherent strength of the Islamic call would affect it. Neither would any opportunist come near it, nor would any pious person keep away from it.

But this people were dominated by worldliness, so those who did not understand the nature of the heavenly call used to raise objections of this kind.

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?"﴾ (43:31).

Therefore the Qur'an rejected their superficial objection to this great mercy of Allah. It is for Allah to choose for His mercy whomever He wills. As for these people, they have blended the values of worldliness and jahiliyyah with the heavenly values of Allah. They are looking at the Islamic call through the eyes of their worldliness, whereas that call is being given for the worship of God and for accountability in the Hereafter.

﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ ... ﴿better than what they amass﴾ (43:32). "We have apportioned among them their means of livelihood in the life of this world, and some of them We have raised above others in degrees so that they may make use of one another. And your Lord's mercy is better than the wealth they gather." That is, it is strange that these people now wish to apportion prophethood themselves, whereas what do they have to do with the mercy and prophethood of Allah? Their real position is that they do not own anything; they do not even own their own provision. That is, even for the brief life of this world their provision is not in their control; it too is apportioned by Us. We apportion it by Our wisdom and planning, and this apportionment of Ours is for the development and flourishing of this earth.

In this world, provision is given to people according to their capacities, according to the conditions of life, and according to the relations of individuals in society. It is distributed among the members of society in accordance with various factors. The system of distribution of provision differs in every society; it changes in every age; every society differs from another; and it depends upon general conditions and the mutual relations of the members of society. But what has been present in the distribution of provision in every age and every society is that there has been difference in the distribution of provision, to the extent that even in artificial societies, whose very aim is to increase production and distribute equally, there is difference in the distribution of provision.

The causes of inequality in provision have differed among different societies, but the difference in the quantity of provision has never disappeared. Even in those artificial societies which claim complete equality, provision differs, and ﴿We have raised some of them above others﴾ (43:32).

In all societies, the causes of differences in degrees of provision have been different, but the wisdom behind it has always been the same.

﴿So that some of them may take others into service﴾ (43:32). That is, some people take others under their subordination and make use of their services. In this world, when the wheel of economy turns, some people sell services and some buy them; thus some become subservient to others. Here, for subjugation (taskhīr) it is not necessary that one nature be superior and the other inferior, or that one person be the slave of another. If this were taken, it would be a very simplistic meaning of the word, and it would not reach the level of Allah's eternal and exalted speech. The meaning of Allah's command is above any change, even though however much the conditions of human society may change, it is not such a meaning that what applied to past conditions is one thing and what applies to coming conditions is another. The real meaning is that all human beings are subservient to one another, and the cycle of life and economy turns everyone around. In every state and every condition, people are dependent on and compelled toward one another. Each person's means of provision are determined: some have wide means and some have limited ones. One person is engaged in amassing wealth, so that he may eat from it himself and also give to others, and both are subservient to one another. The difference in the means of provision between the two has made them needy of and subservient to one another. In the cycle of life, and especially of economic life, people depend on one another: the labourer depends on the engineer and the engineer depends on the owner; the engineer and the labourer both depend on the owner, and the owner depends on both the engineer and the labourer. Each, according to his capacity, is engaged in fulfilling the duty of khilāfah of Allah on this earth, and is subservient. All this has been established through cooperation in the system of provision: some need services and some have them to sell.

Some people who are proponents of self-made theories raise many objections against Islam and its economic system in the light of this verse, and then some Muslims cringe before this verse, and their manner is as if this were an accusation against Islam, and they refute it by saying that Islam does not believe in degrees of distinction in provision, and that difference of degrees in provision is a slander against Islam.

I think the time has now come for Muslims to speak about Islam quite openly and plainly. Without being influenced by those self-made theories and without adopting a defensive posture, they should say clearly that difference in degrees of provision is a reality which Islam allows, and that people will always differ in their means of provision.

The truth is that the natural and psychological condition of man rests upon this very difference. People have been given capacities of different levels by the Creator of the universe. Each person can work according to his capacity, and this difference and gradation of degrees is necessary also so that each person may play a completely distinct role in fulfilling the duty of khilāfah of Allah on this earth. If all people had been created in the manner in which a single advertisement is printed from a press, or a single copy of a book is produced, then this collective form of life in this world would not exist, and many necessary tasks would remain undone, for which no capable person would be available to carry them out. Allah, who created life and arranged for its continuance, has given every person a role and every task a person, "to each has been assigned a task." Then, according to each person's performance, his provision too differs; but there is no difference of degrees which is a zandaqah (heresy). This is the fundamental principle. As for how much difference there should be in the provision of people of different abilities, this depends on the particular system, the particular society and the particular conditions of each country. But this natural principle cannot be rejected anywhere: that there should be a difference of degrees, and so life should develop.

That is why the followers of these artificial systems of economy, who made loud claims of equality, did not establish, and could not establish, equality in the salaries of labourers, engineers and managers. Although they employed the greatest of coercion to bring their system into operation, in the end these people were defeated by the eternal principle of Allah. For the law of Allah rests upon the extremely firm order of life present in this universe. (Sayyid Qutb: Would that you had been alive and seen these artificial creeds collapse with a crash in Russia!) And the system which Allah has indicated for the life of this world is where Allah's mercy lies.

﴿And your Lord's mercy is better than what they amass﴾ (43:32). It is for Allah to choose for His mercy whomever He wills, because Allah alone knows who is fit for which office. Moreover, the mercy of Allah is not tied to the suitability of the economic system present in this world; those are worldly values. In Allah's sight it is no great achievement for someone to amass a very large fortune, since in amassing wealth good doers and wrongdoers have equal opportunities, and righteous and wicked have equal opportunities in it. But for the mercy of Allah (prophethood), the most outstanding people are selected, and only Allah knows this matter.

In the sight of Allah, this world and its wealth are so base and so worthless that, if there were no fear that all people would become disbelievers, Allah would have showered wealth upon the disbelievers here.

﴿And had it not been that all people would have become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses and staircases by which they ascend, and doors for their houses, and couches on which they recline, and adornments of gold. And all this is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world; and the Hereafter with your Lord is only for the righteous﴾ (43:33–35).

Allah knows that His creatures are weak, and how greatly they are swayed by the wealth and riches of this world. Were it not so, Allah would have filled with abundance from this base and contemptible world those who deny His great mercy: their houses, their roofs, their doors, and their furniture would all be of gold and silver. Their homes would have great gates, and the couches on which they sat would have large cushions, and these would be of gold, silver and other precious metals. All this worldly splendour would be handed over to these disbelievers.

﴿And all that is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾ (43:35). That is, the perishable goods, which do not go beyond the limits of this world. This world too is of little value and brief, and human life upon it is brief as well.

﴿But the Hereafter, with your Lord, is for the God-fearing﴾ (43:35). And these people are honoured in Allah's sight because of their taqwa (God-consciousness). Therefore He has prepared for them rewards that are most honourable and precious. And these are more lasting and of greater worth than the perishable goods of this world. Allah will also grant them, on the Day of Resurrection, a distinguished station in comparison with the disbelievers who deny the Most Merciful. As for these disbelievers, Allah gives them the enjoyment of life in the measure with which animals are given fodder.

The truth is that this equipment of worldly life, whose example Allah has given here, dazzles the eyes of many people of this world. When believers see the wealth of wicked and sinful people in their hands, and then see that the hands of Allah's righteous servants are empty of it, or they see that these righteous people lead lives of hardship, distress and straitened means, while these wicked people, relying on their wealth, enjoy power, dominion and authority, they fall into trial. Allah knows that this trial has a great effect on people, but Allah teaches that these things are extremely base, temporary and of little value. And what Allah has prepared for the God-fearing in His presence is beyond imagination. It is for righteous people. In this way the heart of the believer becomes content with the condition that Allah has chosen for the righteous, or for the wicked.

The objection of these people was that Allah had chosen for prophethood a person who did not possess worldly wealth. They measure the worth of people by their authority, their wealth and their status. The answer given to them is that in Allah's sight these things are base and perishable. They are found in abundance among the most wicked of Allah's creatures and among the most hateful of Allah's people. Therefore wealth is not, in Allah's sight, a proof of nearness, rank or the pleasure of God.

Thus the Qur'an places everything in its proper place and correct position. It explains Allah's laws regarding the distribution of sustenance, namely that this is the system of distribution of wealth in this world. It also clarifies what values Allah holds in this matter. All these matters have been stated in the context that these people objected to the Prophetic mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) from this angle: that Allah had passed over the chiefs of Makkah and Ta'if and made Muhammad (ﷺ) a prophet, though in terms of wealth he was an ordinary man.

Thus, in this connection, fundamental and comprehensive principles have been laid down concerning wealth and poverty for the Islamic economic system, and these will undergo no change and no alteration is possible in them. The variety of life, the difference of systems, the difference of ideologies, and the difference of societies and communities will affect none of these principles, because there are certain permanent values in life, and life moves within their sphere. It cannot go outside their sphere. Those whom changing circumstances blind to these permanent values, so that they cannot see them, cannot grasp Allah's permanent economic principle and economic rule. (They have understood this after the collapse of Russia.) The Islamic system is in truth a beautiful blend of stability and change. Its economic system contains principles that change and principles that do not change. But those who do not understand this truth suppose that change and transformation are the essential feature of the progress of life. This change and revolution occurs both in the reality of things and in their form, and these people claim that stable and fixed principles cannot function alongside such change and transformation. These people deny that any permanent law of economics could exist other than change and transformation. They say: "Stability is only change in the age." These people accept only the law of change. Although they employed the greatest of coercion to bring their system into operation, in the end these people were defeated by the eternal principle of Allah. For the law of Allah rests upon the extremely firm order of life present in this universe. (Sayyid Qutb: Would that you had been alive and seen these artificial creeds collapse with a crash in Russia!) And the system which Allah has indicated for the life of this world is where Allah's mercy lies.

﴿And your Lord's mercy is better than what they amass﴾ (43:32). It is for Allah to choose for His mercy whomever He wills, because Allah alone knows who is fit for which office. Moreover, the mercy of Allah is not tied to the suitability of the economic system present in this world; those are worldly values. In Allah's sight it is no great achievement for someone to amass a very large fortune, since in amassing wealth good doers and wrongdoers have equal opportunities, and righteous and wicked have equal opportunities in it. But for the mercy of Allah (prophethood), the most outstanding people are selected, and only Allah knows this matter.

In the sight of Allah, this world and its wealth are so base and so worthless that, if there were no fear that all people would become disbelievers, Allah would have showered wealth upon the disbelievers here.

﴿And had it not been that all people would have become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses and staircases by which they ascend, and doors for their houses, and couches on which they recline, and adornments of gold. And all this is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world; and the Hereafter with your Lord is only for the righteous﴾ (43:33–35).

Allah knows that His creatures are weak, and how greatly they are swayed by the wealth and riches of this world. Were it not so, Allah would have filled with abundance from this base and contemptible world those who deny His great mercy: their houses, their roofs, their doors, and their furniture would all be of gold and silver. Their homes would have great gates, and the couches on which they sat would have large cushions, and these would be of gold, silver and other precious metals. All this worldly splendour would be handed over to these disbelievers.

﴿And all that is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾ (43:35). That is, the perishable goods, which do not go beyond the limits of this world. This world too is of little value and brief, and human life upon it is brief as well.

﴿But the Hereafter, with your Lord, is for the God-fearing﴾ (43:35). And these people are honoured in Allah's sight because of their taqwa (God-consciousness). Therefore He has prepared for them rewards that are most honourable and precious. And these are more lasting and of greater worth than the perishable goods of this world. Allah will also grant them, on the Day of Resurrection, a distinguished station in comparison with the disbelievers who deny the Most Merciful. As for these disbelievers, Allah gives them the enjoyment of life in the measure with which animals are given fodder.

The truth is that this equipment of worldly life, whose example Allah has given here, dazzles the eyes of many people of this world. When believers see the wealth of wicked and sinful people in their hands, and then see that the hands of Allah's righteous servants are empty of it, or they see that these righteous people lead lives of hardship, distress and straitened means, while these wicked people, relying on their wealth, enjoy power, dominion and authority, they fall into trial. Allah knows that this trial has a great effect on people, but Allah teaches that these things are extremely base, temporary and of little value. And what Allah has prepared for the God-fearing in His presence is beyond imagination. It is for righteous people. In this way the heart of the believer becomes content with the condition that Allah has chosen for the righteous, or for the wicked.

The objection of these people was that Allah had chosen for prophethood a person who did not possess worldly wealth. They measure the worth of people by their authority, their wealth and their status. The answer given to them is that in Allah's sight these things are base and perishable. They are found in abundance among the most wicked of Allah's creatures and among the most hateful of Allah's people. Therefore wealth is not, in Allah's sight, a proof of nearness, rank or the pleasure of God.

Thus the Qur'an places everything in its proper place and correct position. It explains Allah's laws regarding the distribution of sustenance, namely that this is the system of distribution of wealth in this world. It also clarifies what values Allah holds in this matter. All these matters have been stated in the context that these people objected to the Prophetic mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) from this angle: that Allah had passed over the chiefs of Makkah and Ta'if and made Muhammad (ﷺ) a prophet, though in terms of wealth he was an ordinary man.

Thus, in this connection, fundamental and comprehensive principles have been laid down concerning wealth and poverty for the Islamic economic system, and these will undergo no change and no alteration is possible in them. The variety of life, the difference of systems, the difference of ideologies, and the difference of societies and communities will affect none of these principles, because there are certain permanent values in life, and life moves within their sphere. It cannot go outside their sphere. Those whom changing circumstances blind to these permanent values, so that they cannot see them, cannot grasp Allah's permanent economic principle and economic rule. (They have understood this after the collapse of Russia.) The Islamic system is in truth a beautiful blend of stability and change. Its economic system contains principles that change and principles that do not change. But those who do not understand this truth suppose that change and transformation are the essential feature of the progress of life. This change and revolution occurs both in the reality of things and in their form, and these people claim that stable and fixed principles cannot function alongside such change and transformation. These people deny that any permanent law of economics could exist other than change and transformation. They say: "Stability is only change in the age." These people accept only the law of change. As for us Muslims, our belief is that in the whole of this universe, stability and change are both inseparable from each other and go together side by side. In some things of this world stability exists as a permanent value, and the great example of this is the very matter under discussion: the inequality in the distribution of sustenance among people is a permanent principle, while the proportion of that inequality always varies. This proportion may change in every country, every society and every age. In the very subject under discussion both examples are present, showing that stability and change both exist in the distribution of economic resources: the inequality is permanent, and the proportion of inequality is variable.

* * *

Having explained that the wealth and goods of this world are nothing in Allah's sight, that they are a base and short-lived provision, and having also shown that the wealth given to wicked and sinful people is no proof of their nobility and honour, and that all the delights of the Hereafter are for the God-fearing, here it is stated what the end will be of those who were given wealth in this world, yet do not remember Allah and turn away from the acts of worship through which blessings would be attained in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 36–39:

Verses 36 to 39

Al-'Asha (العشى) means the inability of the sight to see clearly. Generally this condition occurs when the eyes are confronted with intense light, so that it is impossible to keep them open. Also, because of al-'asha, people with weak sight cannot properly make out things in the darkness of evening. And it also occurs due to a particular illness. The purpose here is heedlessness, turning away from the remembrance of Allah, and erasing from the heart the awareness that Allah is watching.

﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his constant companion.﴾ (43:36) Human nature, by Allah's will, has been so constituted that when the heart becomes heedless of the remembrance of Allah, a devil finds a way to it. He attaches himself to that person, constantly casting whisperings into his heart and making evil appear attractive to him. This condition and its consequence together express beautifully the system of Allah's will. According to Allah's sunnah, as soon as the cause appears, the result comes into view. This decision is already settled according to Allah's knowledge, and it is called qada' and qadar (divine decree and predestination). Moreover, it is the work of devilish evil companions to block their human evil companions from the path of Allah. Thus these people think that they are upon guidance.

﴿And they indeed bar them from the way, while they think that they are rightly guided.﴾ (43:37) It is an exceedingly evil treatment by one friend toward another: to block him from the straight path, put him onto a wrong road, and keep him so heedless that this human friend never even considers that he is mistaken, but instead keeps assuring him that he is walking on the straight path, until he meets a bad end. The verb here is in the present tense to express the continuity of this action: liyasuddunahum, "they bar them," and yahsabun, "they suppose." One can see, indeed other people are watching this spectacle, while they themselves, who are heading toward Hell, are unaware of the end, and the path on which they are going will suddenly bring them to an evil end.

﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he will say, "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! What an evil companion you were!"﴾ (43:38) In the twinkling of an eye we pass from the world to the Hereafter; the register of this life is rolled up, and this blindness brings him, in the company of the devil, to the final end. Here he will come to his senses, just as the drunkard's intoxication wears off, and after blindness and stupefaction, he will lift his eyes and look. Now this person will look closely at his companion, who was assuring him that he was leading him onto the right path, but was in fact a guide to destruction and ruin. Therefore, seething with rage, he will say to him:

﴿"Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts!"﴾ (43:38) "Would that we had never met, and that there had been such distances between us." Then the Qur'an says:

﴿"What an evil companion!"﴾ (43:38) A despairing comment on the state of both of them. Then it draws a curtain over this scene.

﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have done wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾ (43:39) The punishment is equal for all, and it cannot be divided among them.

* * * * *

Now the address turns away from these people, leaving them in that evil state where they blame one another, pour out accusations, and curse each other, and the address begins to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that you should not be distressed by the evil end of these people, and should not care about their aversion and disbelief, but should remain firm upon the truth that is coming to you, for the truth has been continuously coming from ancient times, and every Messenger has presented this very same thing.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 40–45:

Verses 40 to 45

This example is repeated again and again in the Holy Qur'an. It comes to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and through it the reality of guidance and misguidance is explained. It also points to the system of Allah's will (mashiyyah) and divine decree (qada' wa qadar) in this matter, and it makes clear that it is not among the duties of any Messenger to bring people to guidance. It shows the limits of the work of the most exalted striver among human beings, that is, the Messenger, and where the divine power and the system of the cosmos extend. And through it there is a very subtle indication of the doctrine of Tawhid: that only what Allah wills takes place.

Afa-anta tusmi'u al-summa aw tahdi al-'umya wa man kana fi dalalin mubin (43:40): "O Prophet (ﷺ), will you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in clear error?" They were neither deaf nor blind, but they were like the deaf and the blind, and they had gone far away into error, and the call and summons had no effect upon them. They neither understood the proofs of guidance, although the duty of the Messenger (ﷺ) was that whoever hears, he should make him understand, and whoever wishes to see, he should show him the right path. When they themselves have rendered these faculties inoperative, and have closed the eyes of their hearts and minds, how can the Messenger (ﷺ) guide them? Then, if they go astray, what responsibility rests upon the Messenger (ﷺ)? You have discharged your duty. Now it is Allah's affair what He does with them after the discharge of your duty.

Fa-immā nadhhabanna bika fa-innā minhum muntaqimun (43:41); Aw nurinnaka alladhi wa'adnahum fa-innā 'alayhim muqtadirun (43:42): "Now, We shall certainly take retribution against them, whether We take you away from the world, or show you with your own eyes the end that We have promised them; We have full power over them." In any case, one of these two situations will surely occur. If Allah takes the Prophet away, then Allah will take revenge upon his deniers; and if, while you are present, that matter comes into existence with which they are being warned, then Allah has the power to bring into existence that which He is warning them of. They can never defeat Allah in any way. In both situations the matter is in the power and will of Allah; it is Allah who is the owner of this call. The Messenger is only the one who conveys the message.

Fa-istamsik bi-alladhi uhiya ilayka innaka 'ala siratin mustaqim (43:43): "So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are upon a straight path." Stay firm in the work in which you are engaged, and walk upon your path. Do not care about the attitude that these people have adopted or will adopt. Walk upon your path fully content. You are surely upon the straight path. This path will not lead you here and there, it has no crookedness in it, and it does not take you away from its destination.

Moreover, the creed and doctrine which you preach is connected with the reality of this whole universe, and Allah is in harmony with the general law upon which this entire universe stands. This doctrine is in line with the great order (namus akbar) of this universe. It does not separate from it, nor is it cut off from it. And this path leads its traveller exactly to his Creator, and it is so straight that the journey also remains most pleasant.

The Prophet (ﷺ) is enjoined to remain firm upon this truth, and after him, the callers of his Ummah whose conduct will serve as a torch of guidance for them, even if they are suffering torments at the hands of the deviators from this path.

Wa innahu ladhikrun laka wa li-qawmika wa sawfa tus'alun (43:44): "And indeed, this Book is a great honour for you and for your people, and soon you will be called to account for it." Here this verse has two meanings: that this Qur'an is a reminder for you and your people, and that you will soon be questioned on the Day of Resurrection; therefore, after this admonition and reminder, you will have no excuse. The second meaning is that this Qur'an is an honour and a renown for you and your people, and this is the meaning which has come to pass.

As far as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is concerned, billions of lips send blessings and peace upon him, and remember him with love day and night, morning and evening; and thus from the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) mission until the Day of Resurrection, billions of people will continue to recite blessings and peace upon him.

As for the people of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the Qur'an came, they had no name or trace in the world. And if they had anything, it was in the form of a marginal note on the book of life, in a corner. It is this very Qur'an through which a great role of the Arabs was determined in human history. It was the Qur'an that made the greater part of the inhabited world subject to them. As long as they held the Qur'an close to their hearts, the world held them in honour; and when they abandoned the Qur'an, the world abandoned them, they became lowly again, and were then thrown to the very back of the caravan of humanity. But when they held the Qur'an to their breast, they were the leaders of the caravan... and this was a great responsibility, the responsibility of humanity; and Allah will soon call you to account about it, why you abandoned this office. Wa sawfa tus'alun (43:44): "and soon you will be questioned." This last meaning is more comprehensive and inclusive, and I incline towards it.

Wa-s'al man arsalna min qablika min rusulina a-ja'alna min duni al-Rahmani alihatan yu'badun (43:45): "Ask those whom We sent before you of Our Messengers: Did We appoint gods other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?" The Qur'an presents this reality here in a most unique manner, in the form that the Messenger of Allah asks the earlier Messengers.

Aja'alna min duni al-Rahmani alihatan yu'badun (43:45): "Did We appoint, apart from the Most Merciful, other gods to be worshipped?" And then the answer to this question from every Messenger is a definite denial. This rhetorical question of denial is extremely strange and effective, and this style is extremely impactful, that is, ask history.

Between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the earlier prophets there are long distances of time and place. Then there are also long distances of life and death: the Prophet is alive, and the earlier prophets have passed away; yet all these distances vanish. When we see that in the whole of human history prophethood is one, the message is one, and the word of Tawhid is also one, even though time and place are far apart, and there are thick veils between life and death, the unity of prophethood erases all these distances and veils. The dead and the living become one; the past and the present become one. This is the manner of expression of the Holy Qur'an, which is subtle and wondrous.

Furthermore, when one looks at the Prophet (ﷺ), the other noble prophets, and their connection with Allah, the distances of near and far vanish here. Before Allah these veils are removed in the twinkling of an eye, and all obstacles and distances are removed and the reality is revealed. The Prophet (ﷺ) asks questions and the prophets answer, as happened on the night of the Mi'raj.

In such matters we should not give importance to the routines and habits of our life, because these familiar things which we see, that a cause is followed by an effect, are not universal rules in relation to Allah. We can only see some traces of this universe and have reached only a very small part of the natural conditions of this universe. There are many realities which lie beyond our structure, our senses and the results we have formulated. When the human soul leaves the realm of these familiar things and natural phenomena and attains detachment, then it becomes very easy for a human being to reach an abstract reality. This perception then becomes easier still, in the way that someone perceives one body by touching another body with his own body.

***

In consolation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding how the chiefs of Quraysh objected to his prophethood and asked why he had been chosen, and how their objection to his selection was based solely upon the base and false values of the world, a passage from the story of Musa (peace be upon him) is brought, in which it is explained that just as his people regarded themselves as great, so too Pharaoh regarded himself as great in opposition to Musa (peace be upon him). Just as they said:

Wa qalu lawla nuzzila hadha al-Qur'anu 'ala rajulin min al-qaryatayni 'azim (43:31): "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon some great man of the two towns?"

Similarly, Pharaoh too took pride in his power, his rule and his wealth, and asked with a boastful manner:

A-laysa li mulku Misra wa hadhihi al-anharu tajri min tahti? Afala tubsirun (43:51): "O people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and do these rivers not flow beneath me? Do you not see?"

And he, who regarded himself as great in comparison with Musa (peace be upon him), did so merely on account of his worldly rank and status and his wealth, although Musa (peace be upon him) was a chosen servant and Prophet of Allah. But he regarded himself as great in worldly terms:

Am ana khayrun min hadha alladhi huwa mahinun wa la yakadu yubin (43:52): "Am I not better than this man who is despised and cannot even express his speech clearly?"

And how similar are the plan of Pharaoh and the plan of the people of Quraysh!

Verses 40 to 45

This example is repeated again and again in the Holy Qur'an. It comes to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and through it the reality of guidance and misguidance is explained. They neither understood the proofs of guidance, although the duty of the Messenger (ﷺ) was that whoever hears, he should make him understand, and whoever wishes to see, he should show him the right path. When they themselves have rendered these faculties inoperative, and have closed the eyes of their hearts and minds, how can the Messenger (ﷺ) guide them? Then, if they go astray, what responsibility rests upon the Messenger (ﷺ)? You have discharged your duty. Now it is Allah's affair what He does with them after the discharge of your duty.

Fa-immā nadhhabanna bika fa-innā minhum muntaqimun (43:41); Aw nurinnaka alladhi wa'adnahum fa-innā 'alayhim muqtadirun (43:42): "Now, We shall certainly take retribution against them, whether We take you away from the world, or show you with your own eyes the end that We have promised them; We have full power over them." In any case, one of these two situations will surely occur. If Allah takes the Prophet away, then Allah will take revenge upon his deniers; and if, while you are present, that matter comes into existence with which they are being warned, then Allah has the power to bring into existence that which He is warning them of. They can never defeat Allah in any way. In both situations the matter is in the power and will of Allah; it is Allah who is the owner of this call. The Messenger is only the one who conveys the message.

Fa-istamsik bi-alladhi uhiya ilayka innaka 'ala siratin mustaqim (43:43): "So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are upon a straight path." Stay firm in the work in which you are engaged, and walk upon your path. Do not care about the attitude that these people have adopted or will adopt. Walk upon your path fully content. Moreover, the creed and doctrine which you preach is connected with the reality of this whole universe, and Allah is in harmony with the general law upon which this entire universe stands. This doctrine is in line with the great order (namus akbar) of this universe. It does not separate from it, nor is it cut off from it. And this path leads its traveller exactly to his Creator, and it is so straight that the journey also remains most pleasant.

The Prophet (ﷺ) is enjoined to remain firm upon this truth, and after him, the callers of his Ummah whose conduct will serve as a torch of guidance for them, even if they are suffering torments at the hands of the deviators from this path.

Wa innahu ladhikrun laka wa li-qawmika wa sawfa tus'alun (43:44): "And indeed, this Book is a great honour for you and for your people, and soon you will be called to account for it." Here this verse has two meanings: that this Qur'an is a reminder for you and your people, and that you will soon be questioned on the Day of Resurrection; therefore, after this admonition and reminder, you will have no excuse. The second meaning is that this Qur'an is an honour and a renown for you and your people, and this is the meaning which has come to pass.

As far as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is concerned, billions of lips send blessings and peace upon him, and remember him with love day and night, morning and evening; and thus from the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) mission until the Day of Resurrection, billions of people will continue to recite blessings and peace upon him.

As for the people of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the Qur'an came, they had no name or trace in the world. And if they had anything, it was in the form of a marginal note on the book of life, in a corner. It is this very Qur'an through which a great role of the Arabs was determined in human history. It was the Qur'an that made the greater part of the inhabited world subject to them. As long as they held the Qur'an close to their hearts, the world held them in honour; and when they abandoned the Qur'an, the world abandoned them, they became lowly again, and were then thrown to the very back of the caravan of humanity. Wa-s'al man arsalna min qablika min rusulina a-ja'alna min duni al-Rahmani alihatan yu'badun (43:45): "Ask those whom We sent before you of Our Messengers: Did We appoint gods other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?" Then there are also long distances of life and death: the Prophet is alive, and the earlier prophets have passed away; yet all these distances vanish. The dead and the living become one; the past and the present become one. This is the manner of expression of the Holy Qur'an, which is subtle and wondrous.

Furthermore, when one looks at the Prophet (ﷺ), the other noble prophets, and their connection with Allah, the distances of near and far vanish here. Before Allah these veils are removed in the twinkling of an eye, and all obstacles and distances are removed and the reality is revealed. The Prophet (ﷺ) asks questions and the prophets answer, as happened on the night of the Mi'raj.

In such matters we should not give importance to the routines and habits of our life, because these familiar things which we see, that a cause is followed by an effect, are not universal rules in relation to Allah. We can only see some traces of this universe and have reached only a very small part of the natural conditions of this universe. There are many realities which lie beyond our structure, our senses and the results we have formulated. When the human soul leaves the realm of these familiar things and natural phenomena and attains detachment, then it becomes very easy for a human being to reach an abstract reality. This perception then becomes easier still, in the way that someone perceives one body by touching another body with his own body.

It shows the limits of the work of the most exalted striver among human beings, that is, the Messenger, and where the divine power and the system of the cosmos extend. And through it there is a very subtle indication of the doctrine of Tawhid: that only what Allah wills takes place.

Afa-anta tusmi'u al-summa aw tahdi al-'umya wa man kana fi dalalin mubin (43:40): "O Prophet (ﷺ), will you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in clear error?" They were neither deaf nor blind, but they were like the deaf and the blind, and they had gone far away into error, and the call and summons had no effect upon them. They neither understood the proofs of guidance, although the duty of the Messenger (ﷺ) was that whoever hears, he should make him understand, and whoever wishes to see, he should show him the right path. When they themselves have rendered these faculties inoperative, and have closed the eyes of their hearts and minds, how can the Messenger (ﷺ) guide them? Then, if they go astray, what responsibility rests upon the Messenger (ﷺ)? You have discharged your duty. Now it is Allah's affair what He does with them after the discharge of your duty.

Fa-immā nadhhabanna bika fa-innā minhum muntaqimun (43:41); Aw nurinnaka alladhi wa'adnahum fa-innā 'alayhim muqtadirun (43:42): "Now, We shall certainly take retribution against them, whether We take you away from the world, or show you with your own eyes the end that We have promised them; We have full power over them." In any case, one of these two situations will surely occur. If Allah takes the Prophet away, then Allah will take revenge upon his deniers; and if, while you are present, that matter comes into existence with which they are being warned, then Allah has the power to bring into existence that which He is warning them of. They can never defeat Allah in any way. In both situations the matter is in the power and will of Allah; it is Allah who is the owner of this call. The Messenger is only the one who conveys the message.

Fa-istamsik bi-alladhi uhiya ilayka innaka 'ala siratin mustaqim (43:43): "So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are upon a straight path." Stay firm in the work in which you are engaged, and walk upon your path. Do not care about the attitude that these people have adopted or will adopt. Walk upon your path fully content. You are surely upon the straight path. This path will not lead you here and there, it has no crookedness in it, and it does not take you away from its destination.

Moreover, the creed and doctrine which you preach is connected with the reality of this whole universe, and Allah is in harmony with the general law upon which this entire universe stands. This doctrine is in line with the great order (namus akbar) of this universe. It does not separate from it, nor is it cut off from it. And this path leads its traveller exactly to his Creator, and it is so straight that the journey also remains most pleasant.

The Prophet (ﷺ) is enjoined to remain firm upon this truth, and after him, the callers of his Ummah whose conduct will serve as a torch of guidance for them, even if they are suffering torments at the hands of the deviators from this path.

Wa innahu ladhikrun laka wa li-qawmika wa sawfa tus'alun (43:44): "And indeed, this Book is a great honour for you and for your people, and soon you will be called to account for it." Here this verse has two meanings: that this Qur'an is a reminder for you and your people, and that you will soon be questioned on the Day of Resurrection; therefore, after this admonition and reminder, you will have no excuse. The second meaning is that this Qur'an is an honour and a renown for you and your people, and this is the meaning which has come to pass.

As far as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is concerned, billions of lips send blessings and peace upon him, and remember him with love day and night, morning and evening; and thus from the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) mission until the Day of Resurrection, billions of people will continue to recite blessings and peace upon him.

It is this very Qur'an through which a great role of the Arabs was determined in human history. It was the Qur'an that made the greater part of the inhabited world subject to them. As long as they held the Qur'an close to their hearts, the world held them in honour; and when they abandoned the Qur'an, the world abandoned them, they became lowly again, and were then thrown to the very back of the caravan of humanity. Between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the earlier prophets there are long distances of time and place. Verses 48 to 50

Here the Qur'an relates a statement of Pharaoh and his courtiers, and what is strange in it is what they say.

﴿And they said: "O sorcerer, invoke your Lord for us by the covenant He has made with you; indeed, we will surely be guided."﴾ (43:49) This is a people caught in a calamity. They have Musa (peace be upon him) invoke Allah so that this calamity may be lifted, yet at the same time they address him as "O sorcerer" and say:

"Invoke your Lord for us by the covenant He has made with you." (43:49) Although Musa (peace be upon him) used to tell them that he was the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, they did not say that he was merely a Messenger of his own Lord. But the real matter was that these miracles had not affected their hearts, nor had the words of the Messenger affected them. They falsely said: "Indeed, we will surely be guided." (43:49)

﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word.﴾ (43:50) Yet sometimes it also happens that, as a result of miracles, the hearts of the common people are affected, and sometimes a matter takes hold in their deluded minds. Now Pharaoh comes forward with the pomp of royal authority and the display of power, with adornment and ostentation, and presents his superficial logic before the masses and seeks to influence the common people. Before a populace with a slave mentality, whose character is generally transformed in an age of oppression and tyranny, he speaks smooth and flattering words, and before them he displays obstinacy through ostentation.

But the real matter was that these miracles had not affected their hearts, nor had the words of the Messenger affected them. They falsely said: "Indeed, we will surely be guided." (43:49)

﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word.﴾ (43:50) Yet sometimes it also happens that, as a result of miracles, the hearts of the common people are affected, and sometimes a matter takes hold in their deluded minds. Now Pharaoh comes forward with the pomp of royal authority and the display of power, with adornment and ostentation, and presents his superficial logic before the masses and seeks to influence the common people. Before a populace with a slave mentality, whose character is generally transformed in an age of oppression and tyranny, he speaks smooth and flattering words, and before them he displays obstinacy through ostentation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 48–50:

Verses 48 to 50

Thus these continuous miracles that were appearing through the hand of Musa (peace be upon him) did not become a means of faith, even though one greater miracle after another was being manifested. This matter confirms the principle of the Qur'an that is repeated again and again: that the heart which is not fit for guidance is never guided through miracles, and that no Messenger can make the deaf hear or show the path to the blind.

Here the Qur'an relates a statement of Pharaoh and his courtiers, and what is strange in it is what they say.

﴿And they said: "O sorcerer, invoke your Lord for us by the covenant He has made with you; indeed, we will surely be guided."﴾ (43:49) This is a people caught in a calamity. They have Musa (peace be upon him) invoke Allah so that this calamity may be lifted, yet at the same time they address him as "O sorcerer" and say:

"Invoke your Lord for us by the covenant He has made with you." (43:49) Although Musa (peace be upon him) used to tell them that he was the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, they did not say that he was merely a Messenger of his own Lord. But the real matter was that these miracles had not affected their hearts, nor had the words of the Messenger affected them. They falsely said: "Indeed, we will surely be guided." (43:49)

﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word.﴾ (43:50) Yet sometimes it also happens that, as a result of miracles, the hearts of the common people are affected, and sometimes a matter takes hold in their deluded minds. Now Pharaoh comes forward with the pomp of royal authority and the display of power, with adornment and ostentation, and presents his superficial logic before the masses and seeks to influence the common people. Before a populace with a slave mentality, whose character is generally transformed in an age of oppression and tyranny, he speaks smooth and flattering words, and before them he displays obstinacy through ostentation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 51–53:

Verses 51 to 53

The kingdom of Egypt, with its Nile canals under Pharaoh's control, was visible to the common people, and it dazzled their eyes. For this reason people were deceived. As for the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, of which Egypt is but a particle, understanding it requires believing hearts, which can grasp this truth and make a comparison between the kingdom of Allah and the kingdom of Egypt.

As for the masses, accustomed to slavery and exploited in every age, the glitter of the worldly life close at hand impresses them. Therefore their gaze, their hearts and their minds are not raised high enough to comprehend the lofty rule and kingship of Allah. This is why Pharaoh presented a glittering picture of progress to these heedless and superficial hearts of the people, and said:

﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself clearly?﴾ (43:52) "Am I better, or this one who is despicable and cannot even state his case clearly?" Here, by "despicable," he meant that he is neither wealthy, nor holds power, nor has any apparent financial standing. By the word "am," he points to the enslaved people of the Children of Israel, and by "cannot state his case clearly" he refers to the fact that before leaving Egypt, Musa (peace be upon him) had a impediment in his speech. That was an earlier condition; otherwise, he no longer had any impediment. Musa (peace be upon him) had made the supplication:

﴿My Lord, expand for me my chest, ease for me my task, and loosen the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech.﴾ (20:25–28) At that time, the knot of his tongue was untied, and he could now state his message.

And the common people's judgment, obviously, would be that Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, who has caused canals to flow in Egypt, is better than Musa (peace be upon him). For Musa (peace be upon him) had only the truth, the message of prophethood, the call to salvation and the path to escape from painful punishment.

﴿Why have bracelets of gold not been bestowed upon him?﴾ (43:53) "Why were golden bracelets not cast upon him?" This is the mentality of the feudal lords: the contemptible worldly paraphernalia is being proposed as a sign of the truth of prophethood. The golden bracelets were made heavier than the miracles that appeared at the hands of Musa (peace be upon him). The intent was that he should have been given the authority of Egypt, since at the coronation of the king of Egypt golden bracelets were placed upon him; this was their custom. Thus he wishes to say that a messenger should hold supreme authority, and that I am the one who holds it.

﴿Or angels came with him, accompanying him?﴾ (43:53) "Or did no retinue of angels come with him?" This was also an objection, related to the glitter of this world, and it affected the common people. This too is a ready-made objection which was raised against every messenger.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 43, verse 54:

Verse No. 54

It is no surprise that dictators regard the common masses as contemptible and worthless. First, they keep every matter hidden from the masses. They conceal the facts from them so that they forget, and so that they never again investigate concerning them. They affect their hearts and minds to such an extent that their personality comes to dominate the minds of the masses. After this, it becomes easy for them to make the masses light-minded. After this, they become obeyed, and the masses go wherever they wish.

However, no dictator can make the masses this light-minded unless he himself is corrupt and wicked and engaged in deviance, and has not held fast to the rope of Allah, and does not weigh matters on the scale of faith. As for the believers, no one can regard them as light, nor can anyone deceive them, nor can they be made into a plaything. This is why the Holy Qur'an tells us that the common people followed Pharaoh because of their wickedness and immorality: 

﴿Fa-istakhaffa qawmahu fa-atha'uhu innahum kanu qawman fasiqin﴾ (43:54) "He made his people light-minded, so they obeyed him; indeed, they were a corrupt people."

Now the stage of their trial, of warning them and of advising them, comes to an end. Allah knows that this people will not believe. Sedition has become widespread, the common masses have followed Pharaoh, and Pharaoh is extremely rebellious, arrogant and proud, and the masses have become blind to the clear miracles, so that this light does not appear to them at all. Now the decision of Allah's punishment comes upon them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 43, verses 55–56:

Verses 55 to 56

This passage presents the wrath, vengeance and destructive action of the Divine Being, and shows that the works performed by His power as a result of His wrath are unparalleled in history.

Falamma asafuna (43:55): "When they angered Us." That is, they provoked Our great displeasure.

Intaqamna minhum faaghraqnahum ajma'in (43:55): "We took vengeance upon them and drowned them all together." Pharaoh, his chiefs and his army.

These were the very people who were destroyed while pursuing Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). He made them an example, so that every oppressor would do the same deed and reach the same end.

Wa mathalan lil-akhirin (43:56): "And an example for later generations." That is, for those who would act as Pharaoh did after him, and for those who, learning of his story, would take a lesson from it.

٭٭٭

Here the thread of the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) ends. This thread resembled the circumstances that the Prophet ﷺ faced against the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers with him confronted them with great steadfastness. Through this story, the idolaters of Arabia are warned that the objections you raise are the same objections that Pharaoh and his people raised, and this was their end.

In this way, the facts stated in this story fully apply to the story of Pharaoh and Musa and to the present circumstances, that is, the circumstances of the Prophet ﷺ and the people of Quraysh. It also becomes clear why this link of the story has been brought in the circumstances described in this surah. Moreover, in accordance with the Divine method of training, this story is also an excellent means of training for the Muslims.

Now the discourse moves from this link of the story of Musa (peace be upon him) to a link of the story of Isa (peace be upon him). This link is brought to make the point that the polytheists used to worship the angels, considering them daughters of God, and the followers of the Messiah worship him, considering him the son of God. This is the last lesson of this surah.

**Lesson 233: At a Glance**

This is the last lesson of this surah. Its subject is also the mythical beliefs of the Arabs, that the angels are the daughters of Allah and that therefore they are worshipped. Here an argument is cited that the polytheists of Makkah used in defence of their baseless beliefs. They did not put forward this argument in search of truth. It was mere pretence and deception.

When they were told that they and the idols they worship would be fuel for Hell, the intended meaning was that the idols you worship, whether they are named after the angels or after someone else, will be there. It did not mean that those whose names you attach to the idols would also be in Hell. In short, when they were told that both the worshippers and the worshipped would be in Hell, some people cited the example of Jesus, son of Mary, since some misguided Christians worshipped him. This was merely a piece of contentious argument on their part. They then said that since the People of the Book worship Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), we are better than them, because we worship the angels. This argument was the best example of *bina' al-batil 'ala al-batil* (building falsehood upon falsehood).

For this reason, an episode from the story of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) is brought here. It explains the reality of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), what his message was, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what differences arose after him.

After this, everyone holding corrupt and polytheistic ideas is warned that the Hour will come suddenly, and then what their condition will be. Next, one of the long scenes of the Day of Resurrection is presented, in which there is a glimpse of the blessings prepared for the pious (*muttaqun*) and a glimpse of the painful punishment prepared for the criminals (*mujrimun*).

In this lesson, the Arab myth that the angels are the daughters of Allah is also refuted. Allah is free of what they attribute to Him. In this connection, some of Allah's attributes are also mentioned, and it is shown that Allah is the absolute owner of the heavens and the earth, of this world and the Hereafter, and that all people will return to Him.

Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is advised to disregard them, turn away from them, and leave them to what they do. They will soon come to know their end. This is an indirect threat that suits those who, out of mere show, engage in obstinate argument and do not speak in order to establish the truth.

**Lesson 233: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 57 to 65**

Ibn Ishaq wrote in his *Sirah* that, as it reached me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the Sacred Precinct with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith also came and sat with them. Several other Quraysh were sitting in the assembly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith raised an objection, and the Messenger (ﷺ) silenced him. After that, he recited this verse to them:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ (21:98)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left that assembly. Then 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari al-Tamimi came and sat down in the assembly. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, when al-Nadr ibn al-Harith stood up, the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib left. Muhammad (ﷺ) thinks that we and all our deities are fuel for Hell." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I meet him, I will argue with him. Ask Muhammad (ﷺ) whether all the deities that are worshipped will be in Hell along with their worshippers. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah, son of Mary." Al-Walid and the others in the assembly were greatly impressed by the words of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari. They thought that he had presented a strong argument and had won the debate. When this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Whoever likes to be worshipped besides Allah will indeed be in Hell along with those who worshipped him. These people are in fact worshipping Satan, who commanded them to worship these elders." At that point this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

That is, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), Prophet 'Uzayr (peace be upon him), and the other rabbis and monks who were worshipped along with them, who remained steadfast in the worship of Allah, but after their deaths people began to worship them and made them *arbab min dun Allah* (lords besides Allah). As for the statement about Jesus (peace be upon him) being worshipped besides Allah, and al-Walid and the others in the assembly being impressed by it, this verse was revealed concerning it:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people raise an outcry.﴾ (43:57)

*Yasuddun* means *yasuddun 'an amrika*, that is, they keep turning away from your call.

Allamah Zamakhshari wrote in his commentary *al-Kashshaf* that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to the Quraysh this verse:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will all be brought.﴾ (21:98)

the people of Quraysh were furious. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari asked: "Muhammad, is this ruling only about our deities and about us, or does it also apply to the other religions?" He replied: "It is for you and your deities, and for all nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have defeated you! Do you not believe that 'Isa ibn Maryam is a prophet, and that you speak well of him and his mother? You also know that the Christians worship him, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the angels are worshipped as well. If all of these are in Hell, then we are ready to go to Hell along with our deities." They laughed loudly and were delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

And this verse was also revealed, the meaning of which is that when 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari cited the example of 'Isa ibn Maryam and debated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), arguing that the Christians also worship 'Isa, then suddenly your people, the Quraysh, began to raise an uproar. They did this because they were very pleased with that argument, since Za'bari had silenced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Just as sometimes people without arguments, when they lose a debate and suddenly find some argument, become very happy.

The word *yasuddun* means "to raise an uproar", but those who read it as *yasudd* (with a *damma* on the *sad*) mean that they turn away from the truth and reject it. Some have said that *yasuddun* derives from *al-sadid*, which means opposition and being cut off. *Yasuddu* and *yasuddu* both occur, just as *ya'kifu* and *ya'kufu* occur.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:58)

The meaning is: in your view, are our deities not better and superior to 'Isa (peace be upon him)? If 'Isa (peace be upon him) is fuel for Hell, then the matter of our deities is easier.

This is the narration of the author of *al-Kashshaf*. We do not know from whom he took it, but in its general content it agrees with the narration of Ibn Ishaq.

From both narrations it appears that these people, in this disputation and wrangling, relied only on outward and verbal obstinacy. For this very reason the Qur'an says:

﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (43:58)

They argue and are very skilled at criticism; they are debaters. They already know well what the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intend, but then they twist the meaning to make it fit their own aim, and then they raise objections, and they object by seizing upon the general wording of the expressions. Yet they could have derived the specific meaning from the teachings of the whole Qur'an. Such general objections are raised only by one who is not sincere, who is wholly cunning, whose thinking is not sound, who is stubborn, and who is always searching for doubts, verbal tricks, and some loophole to exploit. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) always forbade conversation that is merely show without substance, and in which the speaker always wants to make his own point prevail at any cost.

Ibn Jarir narrated through Abu Kurayb, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubadah ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, and from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out while people were engaged in disputation and argument about the Qur'an. He became extremely angry, as though vinegar had been poured on his blessed face (showing sourness of countenance). Then he said: "Do not set some parts of the Qur'an against other parts, for people went astray only when religious disputes and disagreements arose among them." After that he recited:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

There is another possibility in the interpretation of this verse.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:57)

Here there is an indication that, according to their mythical beliefs, they worshipped the angels, and they thought that their worship was better than the worship that the Christians offered to Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). This is because the angels, by their nature and according to their fanciful notions, are closer to Allah. Upon this, the following comment:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

And, as has passed earlier, this is a refutation of Ibn al-Za'bari. The meaning is that citing the worship of the Christians of the Messiah as an example is baseless here. The practice of the Christians is not a proof, because they have turned away from monotheism, just as the polytheists have turned away from monotheism. Therefore there is no difference between the two; all are misguided. Some commentators have pointed to this, and it may also be a comprehensible interpretation. After this comes a comprehensive comment about Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him):

﴿He was none other than a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (43:59)

He is not a deity to be worshipped, just as a group of Christians went astray and began to worship him. He was a servant of Allah upon whom Allah bestowed His favour. If some people have worshipped him, the fault is not his. He was given prophethood and miracles and made a sign of Allah's power for the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel should have followed him and received guidance, but they went astray.

Now the discussion turns to their beliefs concerning the angels. It is explained that the angels, like you, are creatures of Allah. If We wished, We could make the angels your successors on the earth, or make some people angels who would succeed you on the earth.

﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels among you to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ (43:60)

All these matters depend upon the will of Allah. He may do with His creation whatever He wills, but no creature can establish kinship with Allah, nor can any creature reach Allah except through the relationship of creator and creature, or of worshipped and worshipper, or of master and servant.

After this, some decisions are given concerning Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him): that he is, first, a sign of the Hour, the Hour which they deny or about whose coming they have doubt.

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path. And let not Satan hinder you, for he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (43:61–62)

Concerning the descent of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) before the Hour, many hadiths have come. He will descend upon the earth shortly before the Hour, and this verse points to that.

﴿And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

That is, his coming will be knowledge of the nearness of the Hour. Another reading is:

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

Both meanings are correct.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is near that the son of Mary will descend among you as a just ruler. He will break the cross, kill the pig, impose the jizyah, and distribute wealth until no one will accept it, and a single prostration will be better than the world and what is in it." (Agreed upon; also in Abu Dawud and Malik.)

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A group from my community will continue to fight for the truth until the Day of Resurrection, and they will remain victorious until 'Isa ibn Maryam descends. The leader of the Muslims will say to him: 'Come and lead us in prayer.' He will say: 'No. Some of you are leaders over others. Allah has bestowed this honour upon this community.'" (Muslim)

This is an unseen matter, and it has been informed to us by the truthful and trustworthy one (ﷺ), and the Qur'an also points to it. Therefore no person can say anything else about it. Only that is the truth which has come through these two reliable sources, and for us the reliable sources until the Day of Resurrection are these alone.

**Lesson 233: At a Glance**

This is the last lesson of this surah. Its subject is also the mythical beliefs of the Arabs, that the angels are the daughters of Allah and that therefore they are worshipped. Here an argument is cited that the polytheists of Makkah used in defence of their baseless beliefs. They did not put forward this argument in search of truth. It was mere pretence and deception.

When they were told that they and the idols they worship would be fuel for Hell, the intended meaning was that the idols you worship, whether they are named after the angels or after someone else, will be there. It did not mean that those whose names you attach to the idols would also be in Hell. In short, when they were told that both the worshippers and the worshipped would be in Hell, some people cited the example of Jesus, son of Mary, since some misguided Christians worshipped him. This was merely a piece of contentious argument on their part. They then said that since the People of the Book worship Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), we are better than them, because we worship the angels. This argument was the best example of *bina' al-batil 'ala al-batil* (building falsehood upon falsehood).

For this reason, an episode from the story of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) is brought here. It explains the reality of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), what his message was, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what differences arose after him.

After this, everyone holding corrupt and polytheistic ideas is warned that the Hour will come suddenly, and then what their condition will be. Next, one of the long scenes of the Day of Resurrection is presented, in which there is a glimpse of the blessings prepared for the pious (*muttaqun*) and a glimpse of the painful punishment prepared for the criminals (*mujrimun*).

In this lesson, the Arab myth that the angels are the daughters of Allah is also refuted. Allah is free of what they attribute to Him. In this connection, some of Allah's attributes are also mentioned, and it is shown that Allah is the absolute owner of the heavens and the earth, of this world and the Hereafter, and that all people will return to Him.

Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is advised to disregard them, turn away from them, and leave them to what they do. They will soon come to know their end. This is an indirect threat that suits those who, out of mere show, engage in obstinate argument and do not speak in order to establish the truth.
