**Lesson 233: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 57 to 65**

Ibn Ishaq wrote in his *Sirah* that, as it reached me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the Sacred Precinct with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith also came and sat with them. Several other Quraysh were sitting in the assembly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith raised an objection, and the Messenger (ﷺ) silenced him. After that, he recited this verse to them:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ (21:98)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left that assembly. Then 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari al-Tamimi came and sat down in the assembly. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, when al-Nadr ibn al-Harith stood up, the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib left. Muhammad (ﷺ) thinks that we and all our deities are fuel for Hell." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I meet him, I will argue with him. Ask Muhammad (ﷺ) whether all the deities that are worshipped will be in Hell along with their worshippers. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah, son of Mary." Al-Walid and the others in the assembly were greatly impressed by the words of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari. They thought that he had presented a strong argument and had won the debate. When this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Whoever likes to be worshipped besides Allah will indeed be in Hell along with those who worshipped him. These people are in fact worshipping Satan, who commanded them to worship these elders." At that point this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

That is, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), Prophet 'Uzayr (peace be upon him), and the other rabbis and monks who were worshipped along with them, who remained steadfast in the worship of Allah, but after their deaths people began to worship them and made them *arbab min dun Allah* (lords besides Allah). As for the statement about Jesus (peace be upon him) being worshipped besides Allah, and al-Walid and the others in the assembly being impressed by it, this verse was revealed concerning it:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people raise an outcry.﴾ (43:57)

*Yasuddun* means *yasuddun 'an amrika*, that is, they keep turning away from your call.

Allamah Zamakhshari wrote in his commentary *al-Kashshaf* that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to the Quraysh this verse:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will all be brought.﴾ (21:98)

the people of Quraysh were furious. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari asked: "Muhammad, is this ruling only about our deities and about us, or does it also apply to the other religions?" He replied: "It is for you and your deities, and for all nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have defeated you! Do you not believe that 'Isa ibn Maryam is a prophet, and that you speak well of him and his mother? You also know that the Christians worship him, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the angels are worshipped as well. If all of these are in Hell, then we are ready to go to Hell along with our deities." They laughed loudly and were delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

And this verse was also revealed, the meaning of which is that when 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari cited the example of 'Isa ibn Maryam and debated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), arguing that the Christians also worship 'Isa, then suddenly your people, the Quraysh, began to raise an uproar. They did this because they were very pleased with that argument, since Za'bari had silenced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Just as sometimes people without arguments, when they lose a debate and suddenly find some argument, become very happy.

The word *yasuddun* means "to raise an uproar", but those who read it as *yasudd* (with a *damma* on the *sad*) mean that they turn away from the truth and reject it. Some have said that *yasuddun* derives from *al-sadid*, which means opposition and being cut off. *Yasuddu* and *yasuddu* both occur, just as *ya'kifu* and *ya'kufu* occur.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:58)

The meaning is: in your view, are our deities not better and superior to 'Isa (peace be upon him)? If 'Isa (peace be upon him) is fuel for Hell, then the matter of our deities is easier.

This is the narration of the author of *al-Kashshaf*. We do not know from whom he took it, but in its general content it agrees with the narration of Ibn Ishaq.

From both narrations it appears that these people, in this disputation and wrangling, relied only on outward and verbal obstinacy. For this very reason the Qur'an says:

﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (43:58)

They argue and are very skilled at criticism; they are debaters. They already know well what the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intend, but then they twist the meaning to make it fit their own aim, and then they raise objections, and they object by seizing upon the general wording of the expressions. Yet they could have derived the specific meaning from the teachings of the whole Qur'an. Such general objections are raised only by one who is not sincere, who is wholly cunning, whose thinking is not sound, who is stubborn, and who is always searching for doubts, verbal tricks, and some loophole to exploit. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) always forbade conversation that is merely show without substance, and in which the speaker always wants to make his own point prevail at any cost.

Ibn Jarir narrated through Abu Kurayb, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubadah ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, and from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out while people were engaged in disputation and argument about the Qur'an. He became extremely angry, as though vinegar had been poured on his blessed face (showing sourness of countenance). Then he said: "Do not set some parts of the Qur'an against other parts, for people went astray only when religious disputes and disagreements arose among them." After that he recited:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

There is another possibility in the interpretation of this verse.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:57)

Here there is an indication that, according to their mythical beliefs, they worshipped the angels, and they thought that their worship was better than the worship that the Christians offered to Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). This is because the angels, by their nature and according to their fanciful notions, are closer to Allah. Upon this, the following comment:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

And, as has passed earlier, this is a refutation of Ibn al-Za'bari. The meaning is that citing the worship of the Christians of the Messiah as an example is baseless here. The practice of the Christians is not a proof, because they have turned away from monotheism, just as the polytheists have turned away from monotheism. Therefore there is no difference between the two; all are misguided. Some commentators have pointed to this, and it may also be a comprehensible interpretation. After this comes a comprehensive comment about Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him):

﴿He was none other than a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (43:59)

He is not a deity to be worshipped, just as a group of Christians went astray and began to worship him. He was a servant of Allah upon whom Allah bestowed His favour. If some people have worshipped him, the fault is not his. He was given prophethood and miracles and made a sign of Allah's power for the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel should have followed him and received guidance, but they went astray.

Now the discussion turns to their beliefs concerning the angels. It is explained that the angels, like you, are creatures of Allah. If We wished, We could make the angels your successors on the earth, or make some people angels who would succeed you on the earth.

﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels among you to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ (43:60)

All these matters depend upon the will of Allah. He may do with His creation whatever He wills, but no creature can establish kinship with Allah, nor can any creature reach Allah except through the relationship of creator and creature, or of worshipped and worshipper, or of master and servant.

After this, some decisions are given concerning Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him): that he is, first, a sign of the Hour, the Hour which they deny or about whose coming they have doubt.

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path. And let not Satan hinder you, for he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (43:61–62)

Concerning the descent of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) before the Hour, many hadiths have come. He will descend upon the earth shortly before the Hour, and this verse points to that.

﴿And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

That is, his coming will be knowledge of the nearness of the Hour. Another reading is:

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

Both meanings are correct.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is near that the son of Mary will descend among you as a just ruler. He will break the cross, kill the pig, impose the jizyah, and distribute wealth until no one will accept it, and a single prostration will be better than the world and what is in it." (Agreed upon; also in Abu Dawud and Malik.)

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A group from my community will continue to fight for the truth until the Day of Resurrection, and they will remain victorious until 'Isa ibn Maryam descends. The leader of the Muslims will say to him: 'Come and lead us in prayer.' He will say: 'No. Some of you are leaders over others. Allah has bestowed this honour upon this community.'" (Muslim)

This is an unseen matter, and it has been informed to us by the truthful and trustworthy one (ﷺ), and the Qur'an also points to it. Therefore no person can say anything else about it. Only that is the truth which has come through these two reliable sources, and for us the reliable sources until the Day of Resurrection are these alone.

**Lesson 233: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 57 to 65**

Ibn Ishaq wrote in his *Sirah* that, as it reached me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the Sacred Precinct with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith also came and sat with them. Several other Quraysh were sitting in the assembly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith raised an objection, and the Messenger (ﷺ) silenced him. After that, he recited this verse to them:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ (21:98)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left that assembly. Then 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari al-Tamimi came and sat down in the assembly. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, when al-Nadr ibn al-Harith stood up, the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib left. Muhammad (ﷺ) thinks that we and all our deities are fuel for Hell." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I meet him, I will argue with him. Ask Muhammad (ﷺ) whether all the deities that are worshipped will be in Hell along with their worshippers. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah, son of Mary." Al-Walid and the others in the assembly were greatly impressed by the words of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari. They thought that he had presented a strong argument and had won the debate. When this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Whoever likes to be worshipped besides Allah will indeed be in Hell along with those who worshipped him. These people are in fact worshipping Satan, who commanded them to worship these elders." At that point this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

That is, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), Prophet 'Uzayr (peace be upon him), and the other rabbis and monks who were worshipped along with them, who remained steadfast in the worship of Allah, but after their deaths people began to worship them and made them *arbab min dun Allah* (lords besides Allah). As for the statement about Jesus (peace be upon him) being worshipped besides Allah, and al-Walid and the others in the assembly being impressed by it, this verse was revealed concerning it:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people raise an outcry.﴾ (43:57)

*Yasuddun* means *yasuddun 'an amrika*, that is, they keep turning away from your call.

Allamah Zamakhshari wrote in his commentary *al-Kashshaf* that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to the Quraysh this verse:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will all be brought.﴾ (21:98)

the people of Quraysh were furious. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari asked: "Muhammad, is this ruling only about our deities and about us, or does it also apply to the other religions?" He replied: "It is for you and your deities, and for all nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have defeated you! Do you not believe that 'Isa ibn Maryam is a prophet, and that you speak well of him and his mother? You also know that the Christians worship him, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the angels are worshipped as well. If all of these are in Hell, then we are ready to go to Hell along with our deities." They laughed loudly and were delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

And this verse was also revealed, the meaning of which is that when 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari cited the example of 'Isa ibn Maryam and debated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), arguing that the Christians also worship 'Isa, then suddenly your people, the Quraysh, began to raise an uproar. They did this because they were very pleased with that argument, since Za'bari had silenced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Just as sometimes people without arguments, when they lose a debate and suddenly find some argument, become very happy.

The word *yasuddun* means "to raise an uproar", but those who read it as *yasudd* (with a *damma* on the *sad*) mean that they turn away from the truth and reject it. Some have said that *yasuddun* derives from *al-sadid*, which means opposition and being cut off. *Yasuddu* and *yasuddu* both occur, just as *ya'kifu* and *ya'kufu* occur.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:58)

The meaning is: in your view, are our deities not better and superior to 'Isa (peace be upon him)? If 'Isa (peace be upon him) is fuel for Hell, then the matter of our deities is easier.

This is the narration of the author of *al-Kashshaf*. We do not know from whom he took it, but in its general content it agrees with the narration of Ibn Ishaq.

﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (43:58)

They already know well what the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intend, but then they twist the meaning to make it fit their own aim, and then they raise objections, and they object by seizing upon the general wording of the expressions. Yet they could have derived the specific meaning from the teachings of the whole Qur'an. Such general objections are raised only by one who is not sincere, who is wholly cunning, whose thinking is not sound, who is stubborn, and who is always searching for doubts, verbal tricks, and some loophole to exploit. There is another possibility in the interpretation of this verse.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:57)

Here there is an indication that, according to their mythical beliefs, they worshipped the angels, and they thought that their worship was better than the worship that the Christians offered to Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). ﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

﴿He was none other than a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (43:59)

The Children of Israel should have followed him and received guidance, but they went astray.

Now the discussion turns to their beliefs concerning the angels. It is explained that the angels, like you, are creatures of Allah. If We wished, We could make the angels your successors on the earth, or make some people angels who would succeed you on the earth.

﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels among you to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ (43:60)

All these matters depend upon the will of Allah. He may do with His creation whatever He wills, but no creature can establish kinship with Allah, nor can any creature reach Allah except through the relationship of creator and creature, or of worshipped and worshipper, or of master and servant.

After this, some decisions are given concerning Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him): that he is, first, a sign of the Hour, the Hour which they deny or about whose coming they have doubt.

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path. And let not Satan hinder you, for he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (43:61–62)

Concerning the descent of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) before the Hour, many hadiths have come. He will descend upon the earth shortly before the Hour, and this verse points to that.

﴿And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

That is, his coming will be knowledge of the nearness of the Hour. Another reading is:

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

Both meanings are correct.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is near that the son of Mary will descend among you as a just ruler. He will break the cross, kill the pig, impose the jizyah, and distribute wealth until no one will accept it, and a single prostration will be better than the world and what is in it." (Agreed upon; also in Abu Dawud and Malik.)

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A group from my community will continue to fight for the truth until the Day of Resurrection, and they will remain victorious until 'Isa ibn Maryam descends. This is an unseen matter, and it has been informed to us by the truthful and trustworthy one (ﷺ), and the Qur'an also points to it. Therefore no person can say anything else about it. Only that is the truth which has come through these two reliable sources, and for us the reliable sources until the Day of Resurrection are these alone.

Part 2 of 2 of the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran), on Surah 43, verses 57–65.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is the straight path.﴾ (43:61) These people were doubting the Hour. The Quran invites them to believe in it, and through the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they are called to certainty: obey me, and I will show you the straight path, which is perfectly straight and leads to the desired destination. Those who walk upon it never go astray.

It is explained that those who turn away from the straight path and are cast out from the Divine presence are under the influence of Satan. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more deserving than Satan that he be obeyed.

﴿And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (43:62) The Quran repeatedly points to the continuous struggle that has been going on between the children of Adam and Satan since the time of Adam (peace be upon him). This struggle began in Paradise and continues to this day. And who could be more foolish and heedless than the person who is repeatedly warned that the enemy is lying in ambush, that he has intended harm against you, and yet this person becomes an obedient servant of that enemy instead?

Islam has commanded the human being to remain engaged, throughout his whole life, in this perpetual war against Satan, and has promised for it a reward of such magnitude that it is beyond human imagination. Islam turned the focus of human struggle toward this battle between good and evil, through which the human being becomes a true human being, and through which man has been made a distinguished creature among all creation and given a special temperament. Here, the greatest goal of man has been set as this: that he overcome his open enemy Satan, and thus overcome evil, corruption and every kind of filth, and lay the foundations of goodness on earth, in which people will be well-wishers of one another and will live pure lives.

After this admonition, further information is given about Jesus (peace be upon him): what message he brought, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what happened afterward.

﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of the matters about which you differ; so fear Allah and obey me. Jesus (peace be upon him) came to the people with clear signs. These signs were the miracles that appeared at his hands, and also the words and addresses he delivered to guide people to the right path. He said to his people:

﴿I have come to you with wisdom﴾ (43:63). Whoever is given wisdom has, as it were, become the possessor of abundant good. He is safe from slips and deviation, protected from negligence and shortcoming, and his steps on the right path begin to fall with perfect balance and in light. Moreover, he came to them especially so that he might remove the great division that had arisen among the religious groups at that time. The jurists of the Law of Moses had begun great disagreement, and the people had split into sects and fragments. He called his people to fear Allah and obey him, and he explained the doctrine of Tawhid with great clarity, without any doubt or confusion or complexity.

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:64). He neither claimed to be a deity, nor claimed to be the son of Allah, and in his speech he did not allude anywhere to any relationship with Allah other than the relationship of Lord and servant, and of Creator and creature. He only said that he was a messenger, sent with the straight path, in which there is no crookedness, no slippage, and no deviation. Yet those who came after Jesus (peace be upon him) also became fragments and parties, just as the people before him had been fragments and parties. They created these differences merely through wrongdoing; there was neither justification for the differences nor any basis for doubt.

﴿So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65).

The mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was for the Children of Israel. In that era the Children of Israel were subjects of the Romans. They were waiting for a Redeemer who would come and free them, but when he came, they refused to recognize him, turned to enmity against him, and sought to crucify him.

When he appeared, the Children of Israel were divided into fragments, and there were four major sects:

1. The Sadducees: They were named after Sadoq; he and his family were the priests of the Temple of Solomon. From the time of David and Solomon (peace be upon them) they held this office. According to the Law, it was necessary that their lineage reach Aaron (peace be upon him), the brother of Moses (peace be upon him) and a prophet, because the descendants of Aaron alone were the custodians of the Temple. These people laid great emphasis on the outward form of worship according to their duties, and were strict opponents of any innovation, while in their personal lives they were very indulgent and enjoyed life's pleasures, and they held the belief that there is no Resurrection.

2. The Pharisees: They were strongly opposed to the Sadducees. Their objection to them was that these people laid great emphasis on the outward form of religious rites and worship and denied the Resurrection and the reckoning. They were extremely pious people of a Sufi type, although some of them were overcome by intellectual pride, and Jesus (peace be upon him) did not like their intellectual arrogance. Moreover, he did not like their verbosity either.

3. The third sect was that of the Samaritans: This sect consisted of Jews and Assyrians, and it accepted only the first five books of the Old Testament, considering the rest to be later additions. These five books are known as the Books of Moses, whereas the other sects accepted all the books.

4. They were called Essenes or Essenians: These people were influenced by certain philosophical ideas. They kept themselves separate from the other sects, and subjected themselves to great severity and asceticism, and their community was also very strict in organization.

Apart from these four well-known sects, there were also many individual sects. In short, among the Children of Israel there was severe disagreement and disintegration in their beliefs and conduct, and they were under heavy pressure from the Roman imperial power, and the whole nation was living a life of extreme humiliation and slavery. This was the setting in which a prophecy about a Redeemer had been recorded in their books, that he would come and deliver them.

When Messiah was sent with the doctrine of Tawhid and he made the proclamation:

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:63), and along with it he presented a law that emphasized compassion and spiritual reform, and stressed the spiritual aspect of worship rather than its outward form, then those jurists and Pharisees opposed him, because they laid stress only on the outward forms of worship.

Among the things Jesus (peace be upon him) said about these people, some of his statements are very effective, such as: "They bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger. But all their works they do to be seen of men... and they love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi."

And to the Pharisees and scribes he said: "Woe unto you, blind guides, which strain at a gnat and swallow a camel! You cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess... Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like unto whitewashed tombs, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones and of all uncleanness."

Read these words of Jesus (peace be upon him) and look at the scholars and muftis of your own age: do these very words not apply to them—those who distort religion, the worshippers of rituals, the outwardly pious and the showy?

After this, Jesus (peace be upon him) went to his Lord. Thereafter, differences arose among his followers. In this way they split into sects and fragments. Some made him a deity; some took him to be the son of Allah; some said "Trinity," and the word of Tawhid, for which he had come so that these people might return to their Lord and make religion pure for Allah, was lost from them.

﴿But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65). The idolaters of Arabia came and began to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Jesus (peace be upon him), because the followers of the Messiah had, after him, wrought their mischief and had fabricated countless legends about him.

When he appeared, the Children of Israel were divided into fragments, and there were four major sects:

1. The Sadducees: They were named after Sadoq; he and his family were the priests of the Temple of Solomon. From the time of David and Solomon (peace be upon them) they held this office. These people laid great emphasis on the outward form of worship according to their duties, and were strict opponents of any innovation, while in their personal lives they were very indulgent and enjoyed life's pleasures, and they held the belief that there is no Resurrection.

2. The Pharisees: They were strongly opposed to the Sadducees. Their objection to them was that these people laid great emphasis on the outward form of religious rites and worship and denied the Resurrection and the reckoning. Apart from these four well-known sects, there were also many individual sects. In short, among the Children of Israel there was severe disagreement and disintegration in their beliefs and conduct, and they were under heavy pressure from the Roman imperial power, and the whole nation was living a life of extreme humiliation and slavery. This was the setting in which a prophecy about a Redeemer had been recorded in their books, that he would come and deliver them.

For you are like unto whitewashed tombs, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones and of all uncleanness."

Read these words of Jesus (peace be upon him) and look at the scholars and muftis of your own age: do these very words not apply to them—those who distort religion, the worshippers of rituals, the outwardly pious and the showy?

Some made him a deity; some took him to be the son of Allah; some said "Trinity," and the word of Tawhid, for which he had come so that these people might return to their Lord and make religion pure for Allah, was lost from them.

The idolaters of Arabia came and began to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Jesus (peace be upon him), because the followers of the Messiah had, after him, wrought their mischief and had fabricated countless legends about him.

**Lesson 233: At a Glance**

This is the last lesson of this surah. Its subject is also the mythical beliefs of the Arabs, that the angels are the daughters of Allah and that therefore they are worshipped. Here an argument is cited that the polytheists of Makkah used in defence of their baseless beliefs. They did not put forward this argument in search of truth. It was mere pretence and deception.

When they were told that they and the idols they worship would be fuel for Hell, the intended meaning was that the idols you worship, whether they are named after the angels or after someone else, will be there. It did not mean that those whose names you attach to the idols would also be in Hell. In short, when they were told that both the worshippers and the worshipped would be in Hell, some people cited the example of Jesus, son of Mary, since some misguided Christians worshipped him. This was merely a piece of contentious argument on their part. They then said that since the People of the Book worship Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), we are better than them, because we worship the angels. This argument was the best example of *bina' al-batil 'ala al-batil* (building falsehood upon falsehood).

For this reason, an episode from the story of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) is brought here. It explains the reality of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), what his message was, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what differences arose after him.

After this, everyone holding corrupt and polytheistic ideas is warned that the Hour will come suddenly, and then what their condition will be. Next, one of the long scenes of the Day of Resurrection is presented, in which there is a glimpse of the blessings prepared for the pious (*muttaqun*) and a glimpse of the painful punishment prepared for the criminals (*mujrimun*).

In this lesson, the Arab myth that the angels are the daughters of Allah is also refuted. Allah is free of what they attribute to Him. In this connection, some of Allah's attributes are also mentioned, and it is shown that Allah is the absolute owner of the heavens and the earth, of this world and the Hereafter, and that all people will return to Him.

Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is advised to disregard them, turn away from them, and leave them to what they do. They will soon come to know their end. This is an indirect threat that suits those who, out of mere show, engage in obstinate argument and do not speak in order to establish the truth.

**Lesson 233: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 57 to 65**

Ibn Ishaq wrote in his *Sirah* that, as it reached me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the Sacred Precinct with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith also came and sat with them. Several other Quraysh were sitting in the assembly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith raised an objection, and the Messenger (ﷺ) silenced him. After that, he recited this verse to them:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ (21:98)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left that assembly. Then 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari al-Tamimi came and sat down in the assembly. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, when al-Nadr ibn al-Harith stood up, the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib left. Muhammad (ﷺ) thinks that we and all our deities are fuel for Hell." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I meet him, I will argue with him. Ask Muhammad (ﷺ) whether all the deities that are worshipped will be in Hell along with their worshippers. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah, son of Mary." Al-Walid and the others in the assembly were greatly impressed by the words of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari. They thought that he had presented a strong argument and had won the debate. When this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Whoever likes to be worshipped besides Allah will indeed be in Hell along with those who worshipped him. These people are in fact worshipping Satan, who commanded them to worship these elders." At that point this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

That is, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), Prophet 'Uzayr (peace be upon him), and the other rabbis and monks who were worshipped along with them, who remained steadfast in the worship of Allah, but after their deaths people began to worship them and made them *arbab min dun Allah* (lords besides Allah). As for the statement about Jesus (peace be upon him) being worshipped besides Allah, and al-Walid and the others in the assembly being impressed by it, this verse was revealed concerning it:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people raise an outcry.﴾ (43:57)

*Yasuddun* means *yasuddun 'an amrika*, that is, they keep turning away from your call.

Allamah Zamakhshari wrote in his commentary *al-Kashshaf* that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to the Quraysh this verse:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will all be brought.﴾ (21:98)

the people of Quraysh were furious. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari asked: "Muhammad, is this ruling only about our deities and about us, or does it also apply to the other religions?" He replied: "It is for you and your deities, and for all nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have defeated you! Do you not believe that 'Isa ibn Maryam is a prophet, and that you speak well of him and his mother? You also know that the Christians worship him, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the angels are worshipped as well. If all of these are in Hell, then we are ready to go to Hell along with our deities." They laughed loudly and were delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

And this verse was also revealed, the meaning of which is that when 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari cited the example of 'Isa ibn Maryam and debated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), arguing that the Christians also worship 'Isa, then suddenly your people, the Quraysh, began to raise an uproar. They did this because they were very pleased with that argument, since Za'bari had silenced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Just as sometimes people without arguments, when they lose a debate and suddenly find some argument, become very happy.

The word *yasuddun* means "to raise an uproar", but those who read it as *yasudd* (with a *damma* on the *sad*) mean that they turn away from the truth and reject it. Some have said that *yasuddun* derives from *al-sadid*, which means opposition and being cut off. *Yasuddu* and *yasuddu* both occur, just as *ya'kifu* and *ya'kufu* occur.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:58)

The meaning is: in your view, are our deities not better and superior to 'Isa (peace be upon him)? If 'Isa (peace be upon him) is fuel for Hell, then the matter of our deities is easier.

This is the narration of the author of *al-Kashshaf*. We do not know from whom he took it, but in its general content it agrees with the narration of Ibn Ishaq.

﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (43:58)

Such general objections are raised only by one who is not sincere, who is wholly cunning, whose thinking is not sound, who is stubborn, and who is always searching for doubts, verbal tricks, and some loophole to exploit. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) always forbade conversation that is merely show without substance, and in which the speaker always wants to make his own point prevail at any cost.

Read these words of Jesus (peace be upon him) and look at the scholars and muftis of your own age: do these very words not apply to them—those who distort religion, the worshippers of rituals, the outwardly pious and the showy?

**Lesson 233: At a Glance**

This is the last lesson of this surah. Its subject is also the mythical beliefs of the Arabs, that the angels are the daughters of Allah and that therefore they are worshipped. Here an argument is cited that the polytheists of Makkah used in defence of their baseless beliefs. They did not put forward this argument in search of truth. It was mere pretence and deception.

**Lesson 233: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 57 to 65**

Ibn Ishaq wrote in his *Sirah* that, as it reached me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the Sacred Precinct with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith also came and sat with them. Several other Quraysh were sitting in the assembly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith raised an objection, and the Messenger (ﷺ) silenced him. After that, he recited this verse to them:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ (21:98)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left that assembly. Then 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari al-Tamimi came and sat down in the assembly. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, when al-Nadr ibn al-Harith stood up, the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib left. Muhammad (ﷺ) thinks that we and all our deities are fuel for Hell." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I meet him, I will argue with him. Ask Muhammad (ﷺ) whether all the deities that are worshipped will be in Hell along with their worshippers. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah, son of Mary." Al-Walid and the others in the assembly were greatly impressed by the words of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari. They thought that he had presented a strong argument and had won the debate. When this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Whoever likes to be worshipped besides Allah will indeed be in Hell along with those who worshipped him. These people are in fact worshipping Satan, who commanded them to worship these elders." At that point this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

That is, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), Prophet 'Uzayr (peace be upon him), and the other rabbis and monks who were worshipped along with them, who remained steadfast in the worship of Allah, but after their deaths people began to worship them and made them *arbab min dun Allah* (lords besides Allah). As for the statement about Jesus (peace be upon him) being worshipped besides Allah, and al-Walid and the others in the assembly being impressed by it, this verse was revealed concerning it:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people raise an outcry.﴾ (43:57)

*Yasuddun* means *yasuddun 'an amrika*, that is, they keep turning away from your call.

Allamah Zamakhshari wrote in his commentary *al-Kashshaf* that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to the Quraysh this verse:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will all be brought.﴾ (21:98)

the people of Quraysh were furious. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari asked: "Muhammad, is this ruling only about our deities and about us, or does it also apply to the other religions?" He replied: "It is for you and your deities, and for all nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have defeated you! Do you not believe that 'Isa ibn Maryam is a prophet, and that you speak well of him and his mother? You also know that the Christians worship him, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the angels are worshipped as well. If all of these are in Hell, then we are ready to go to Hell along with our deities." They laughed loudly and were delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

And this verse was also revealed, the meaning of which is that when 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari cited the example of 'Isa ibn Maryam and debated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), arguing that the Christians also worship 'Isa, then suddenly your people, the Quraysh, began to raise an uproar. They did this because they were very pleased with that argument, since Za'bari had silenced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Just as sometimes people without arguments, when they lose a debate and suddenly find some argument, become very happy.

The word *yasuddun* means "to raise an uproar", but those who read it as *yasudd* (with a *damma* on the *sad*) mean that they turn away from the truth and reject it. Some have said that *yasuddun* derives from *al-sadid*, which means opposition and being cut off. *Yasuddu* and *yasuddu* both occur, just as *ya'kifu* and *ya'kufu* occur.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:58)

The meaning is: in your view, are our deities not better and superior to 'Isa (peace be upon him)? If 'Isa (peace be upon him) is fuel for Hell, then the matter of our deities is easier.

This is the narration of the author of *al-Kashshaf*. We do not know from whom he took it, but in its general content it agrees with the narration of Ibn Ishaq.

From both narrations it appears that these people, in this disputation and wrangling, relied only on outward and verbal obstinacy. For this very reason the Qur'an says:

﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (43:58)

They argue and are very skilled at criticism; they are debaters. They already know well what the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intend, but then they twist the meaning to make it fit their own aim, and then they raise objections, and they object by seizing upon the general wording of the expressions. Yet they could have derived the specific meaning from the teachings of the whole Qur'an. Such general objections are raised only by one who is not sincere, who is wholly cunning, whose thinking is not sound, who is stubborn, and who is always searching for doubts, verbal tricks, and some loophole to exploit. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) always forbade conversation that is merely show without substance, and in which the speaker always wants to make his own point prevail at any cost.

Ibn Jarir narrated through Abu Kurayb, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubadah ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, and from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out while people were engaged in disputation and argument about the Qur'an. He became extremely angry, as though vinegar had been poured on his blessed face (showing sourness of countenance). Then he said: "Do not set some parts of the Qur'an against other parts, for people went astray only when religious disputes and disagreements arose among them." After that he recited:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

There is another possibility in the interpretation of this verse.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:57)

Here there is an indication that, according to their mythical beliefs, they worshipped the angels, and they thought that their worship was better than the worship that the Christians offered to Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). This is because the angels, by their nature and according to their fanciful notions, are closer to Allah. Upon this, the following comment:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

And, as has passed earlier, this is a refutation of Ibn al-Za'bari. The meaning is that citing the worship of the Christians of the Messiah as an example is baseless here. The practice of the Christians is not a proof, because they have turned away from monotheism, just as the polytheists have turned away from monotheism. Therefore there is no difference between the two; all are misguided. Some commentators have pointed to this, and it may also be a comprehensible interpretation. After this comes a comprehensive comment about Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him):

﴿He was none other than a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (43:59)

He is not a deity to be worshipped, just as a group of Christians went astray and began to worship him. He was a servant of Allah upon whom Allah bestowed His favour. If some people have worshipped him, the fault is not his. He was given prophethood and miracles and made a sign of Allah's power for the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel should have followed him and received guidance, but they went astray.

Now the discussion turns to their beliefs concerning the angels. It is explained that the angels, like you, are creatures of Allah. If We wished, We could make the angels your successors on the earth, or make some people angels who would succeed you on the earth.

﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels among you to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ (43:60)

All these matters depend upon the will of Allah. He may do with His creation whatever He wills, but no creature can establish kinship with Allah, nor can any creature reach Allah except through the relationship of creator and creature, or of worshipped and worshipper, or of master and servant.

After this, some decisions are given concerning Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him): that he is, first, a sign of the Hour, the Hour which they deny or about whose coming they have doubt.

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path. And let not Satan hinder you, for he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (43:61–62)

Concerning the descent of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) before the Hour, many hadiths have come. He will descend upon the earth shortly before the Hour, and this verse points to that.

﴿And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

That is, his coming will be knowledge of the nearness of the Hour. Another reading is:

﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour.﴾ (43:61)

Both meanings are correct.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is near that the son of Mary will descend among you as a just ruler. He will break the cross, kill the pig, impose the jizyah, and distribute wealth until no one will accept it, and a single prostration will be better than the world and what is in it." (Agreed upon; also in Abu Dawud and Malik.)

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A group from my community will continue to fight for the truth until the Day of Resurrection, and they will remain victorious until 'Isa ibn Maryam descends. The leader of the Muslims will say to him: 'Come and lead us in prayer.' He will say: 'No. Some of you are leaders over others. Allah has bestowed this honour upon this community.'" (Muslim)

This is an unseen matter, and it has been informed to us by the truthful and trustworthy one (ﷺ), and the Qur'an also points to it. Therefore no person can say anything else about it. Only that is the truth which has come through these two reliable sources, and for us the reliable sources until the Day of Resurrection are these alone.

Part 2 of 2 of the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran), on Surah 43, verses 57–65.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is the straight path.﴾ (43:61) These people were doubting the Hour. The Quran invites them to believe in it, and through the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they are called to certainty: obey me, and I will show you the straight path, which is perfectly straight and leads to the desired destination. Those who walk upon it never go astray.

It is explained that those who turn away from the straight path and are cast out from the Divine presence are under the influence of Satan. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more deserving than Satan that he be obeyed.

﴿And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (43:62) The Quran repeatedly points to the continuous struggle that has been going on between the children of Adam and Satan since the time of Adam (peace be upon him). This struggle began in Paradise and continues to this day. And who could be more foolish and heedless than the person who is repeatedly warned that the enemy is lying in ambush, that he has intended harm against you, and yet this person becomes an obedient servant of that enemy instead?

Islam has commanded the human being to remain engaged, throughout his whole life, in this perpetual war against Satan, and has promised for it a reward of such magnitude that it is beyond human imagination. Islam turned the focus of human struggle toward this battle between good and evil, through which the human being becomes a true human being, and through which man has been made a distinguished creature among all creation and given a special temperament. Here, the greatest goal of man has been set as this: that he overcome his open enemy Satan, and thus overcome evil, corruption and every kind of filth, and lay the foundations of goodness on earth, in which people will be well-wishers of one another and will live pure lives.

After this admonition, further information is given about Jesus (peace be upon him): what message he brought, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what happened afterward.

﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of the matters about which you differ; so fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path." But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day.﴾ (43:63–65)

Jesus (peace be upon him) came to the people with clear signs. These signs were the miracles that appeared at his hands, and also the words and addresses he delivered to guide people to the right path. He said to his people:

﴿I have come to you with wisdom﴾ (43:63). Whoever is given wisdom has, as it were, become the possessor of abundant good. He is safe from slips and deviation, protected from negligence and shortcoming, and his steps on the right path begin to fall with perfect balance and in light. Moreover, he came to them especially so that he might remove the great division that had arisen among the religious groups at that time. The jurists of the Law of Moses had begun great disagreement, and the people had split into sects and fragments. He called his people to fear Allah and obey him, and he explained the doctrine of Tawhid with great clarity, without any doubt or confusion or complexity.

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:64). He neither claimed to be a deity, nor claimed to be the son of Allah, and in his speech he did not allude anywhere to any relationship with Allah other than the relationship of Lord and servant, and of Creator and creature. He only said that he was a messenger, sent with the straight path, in which there is no crookedness, no slippage, and no deviation. Yet those who came after Jesus (peace be upon him) also became fragments and parties, just as the people before him had been fragments and parties. They created these differences merely through wrongdoing; there was neither justification for the differences nor any basis for doubt.

﴿So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65).

The mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was for the Children of Israel. In that era the Children of Israel were subjects of the Romans. They were waiting for a Redeemer who would come and free them, but when he came, they refused to recognize him, turned to enmity against him, and sought to crucify him.

When he appeared, the Children of Israel were divided into fragments, and there were four major sects:

1. The Sadducees: They were named after Sadoq; he and his family were the priests of the Temple of Solomon. From the time of David and Solomon (peace be upon them) they held this office. According to the Law, it was necessary that their lineage reach Aaron (peace be upon him), the brother of Moses (peace be upon him) and a prophet, because the descendants of Aaron alone were the custodians of the Temple. These people laid great emphasis on the outward form of worship according to their duties, and were strict opponents of any innovation, while in their personal lives they were very indulgent and enjoyed life's pleasures, and they held the belief that there is no Resurrection.

2. The Pharisees: They were strongly opposed to the Sadducees. Their objection to them was that these people laid great emphasis on the outward form of religious rites and worship and denied the Resurrection and the reckoning. They were extremely pious people of a Sufi type, although some of them were overcome by intellectual pride, and Jesus (peace be upon him) did not like their intellectual arrogance. Moreover, he did not like their verbosity either.

3. The third sect was that of the Samaritans: This sect consisted of Jews and Assyrians, and it accepted only the first five books of the Old Testament, considering the rest to be later additions. These five books are known as the Books of Moses, whereas the other sects accepted all the books.

4. They were called Essenes or Essenians: These people were influenced by certain philosophical ideas. They kept themselves separate from the other sects, and subjected themselves to great severity and asceticism, and their community was also very strict in organization.

Apart from these four well-known sects, there were also many individual sects. In short, among the Children of Israel there was severe disagreement and disintegration in their beliefs and conduct, and they were under heavy pressure from the Roman imperial power, and the whole nation was living a life of extreme humiliation and slavery. This was the setting in which a prophecy about a Redeemer had been recorded in their books, that he would come and deliver them.

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:63), and along with it he presented a law that emphasized compassion and spiritual reform, and stressed the spiritual aspect of worship rather than its outward form, then those jurists and Pharisees opposed him, because they laid stress only on the outward forms of worship.

Among the things Jesus (peace be upon him) said about these people, some of his statements are very effective, such as: "They bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger. But all their works they do to be seen of men... and they love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi."

And to the Pharisees and scribes he said: "Woe unto you, blind guides, which strain at a gnat and swallow a camel! You cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess... Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like unto whitewashed tombs, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones and of all uncleanness."

Read these words of Jesus (peace be upon him) and look at the scholars and muftis of your own age: do these very words not apply to them—those who distort religion, the worshippers of rituals, the outwardly pious and the showy?

After this, Jesus (peace be upon him) went to his Lord. Thereafter, differences arose among his followers. In this way they split into sects and fragments. Some made him a deity; some took him to be the son of Allah; some said "Trinity," and the word of Tawhid, for which he had come so that these people might return to their Lord and make religion pure for Allah, was lost from them.

﴿But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65). The idolaters of Arabia came and began to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Jesus (peace be upon him), because the followers of the Messiah had, after him, wrought their mischief and had fabricated countless legends about him.

He called his people to fear Allah and obey him, and he explained the doctrine of Tawhid with great clarity, without any doubt or confusion or complexity.

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:64). He only said that he was a messenger, sent with the straight path, in which there is no crookedness, no slippage, and no deviation. Yet those who came after Jesus (peace be upon him) also became fragments and parties, just as the people before him had been fragments and parties. They created these differences merely through wrongdoing; there was neither justification for the differences nor any basis for doubt.

﴿So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65).

They were waiting for a Redeemer who would come and free them, but when he came, they refused to recognize him, turned to enmity against him, and sought to crucify him.

When he appeared, the Children of Israel were divided into fragments, and there were four major sects:

1. The Sadducees: They were named after Sadoq; he and his family were the priests of the Temple of Solomon. From the time of David and Solomon (peace be upon them) they held this office. According to the Law, it was necessary that their lineage reach Aaron (peace be upon him), the brother of Moses (peace be upon him) and a prophet, because the descendants of Aaron alone were the custodians of the Temple. These people laid great emphasis on the outward form of worship according to their duties, and were strict opponents of any innovation, while in their personal lives they were very indulgent and enjoyed life's pleasures, and they held the belief that there is no Resurrection.

2. The Pharisees: They were strongly opposed to the Sadducees. Their objection to them was that these people laid great emphasis on the outward form of religious rites and worship and denied the Resurrection and the reckoning. They were extremely pious people of a Sufi type, although some of them were overcome by intellectual pride, and Jesus (peace be upon him) did not like their intellectual arrogance. Moreover, he did not like their verbosity either.

3. The third sect was that of the Samaritans: This sect consisted of Jews and Assyrians, and it accepted only the first five books of the Old Testament, considering the rest to be later additions. These five books are known as the Books of Moses, whereas the other sects accepted all the books.

4. They were called Essenes or Essenians: These people were influenced by certain philosophical ideas. They kept themselves separate from the other sects, and subjected themselves to great severity and asceticism, and their community was also very strict in organization.

Apart from these four well-known sects, there were also many individual sects. In short, among the Children of Israel there was severe disagreement and disintegration in their beliefs and conduct, and they were under heavy pressure from the Roman imperial power, and the whole nation was living a life of extreme humiliation and slavery. This was the setting in which a prophecy about a Redeemer had been recorded in their books, that he would come and deliver them.

When Messiah was sent with the doctrine of Tawhid and he made the proclamation:

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:63), and along with it he presented a law that emphasized compassion and spiritual reform, and stressed the spiritual aspect of worship rather than its outward form, then those jurists and Pharisees opposed him, because they laid stress only on the outward forms of worship.

Among the things Jesus (peace be upon him) said about these people, some of his statements are very effective, such as: "They bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger. You cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess... Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like unto whitewashed tombs, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones and of all uncleanness."

Read these words of Jesus (peace be upon him) and look at the scholars and muftis of your own age: do these very words not apply to them—those who distort religion, the worshippers of rituals, the outwardly pious and the showy?

After this, Jesus (peace be upon him) went to his Lord. Thereafter, differences arose among his followers. In this way they split into sects and fragments. Some made him a deity; some took him to be the son of Allah; some said "Trinity," and the word of Tawhid, for which he had come so that these people might return to their Lord and make religion pure for Allah, was lost from them.

﴿But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65). The idolaters of Arabia came and began to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Jesus (peace be upon him), because the followers of the Messiah had, after him, wrought their mischief and had fabricated countless legends about him.

**Lesson 233: At a Glance**

This is the last lesson of this surah. Its subject is also the mythical beliefs of the Arabs, that the angels are the daughters of Allah and that therefore they are worshipped. Here an argument is cited that the polytheists of Makkah used in defence of their baseless beliefs. They did not put forward this argument in search of truth. It was mere pretence and deception.

When they were told that they and the idols they worship would be fuel for Hell, the intended meaning was that the idols you worship, whether they are named after the angels or after someone else, will be there. It did not mean that those whose names you attach to the idols would also be in Hell. In short, when they were told that both the worshippers and the worshipped would be in Hell, some people cited the example of Jesus, son of Mary, since some misguided Christians worshipped him. This was merely a piece of contentious argument on their part. They then said that since the People of the Book worship Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), we are better than them, because we worship the angels. This argument was the best example of *bina' al-batil 'ala al-batil* (building falsehood upon falsehood).

For this reason, an episode from the story of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) is brought here. It explains the reality of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), what his message was, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what differences arose after him.

After this, everyone holding corrupt and polytheistic ideas is warned that the Hour will come suddenly, and then what their condition will be. Next, one of the long scenes of the Day of Resurrection is presented, in which there is a glimpse of the blessings prepared for the pious (*muttaqun*) and a glimpse of the painful punishment prepared for the criminals (*mujrimun*).

In this lesson, the Arab myth that the angels are the daughters of Allah is also refuted. Allah is free of what they attribute to Him. In this connection, some of Allah's attributes are also mentioned, and it is shown that Allah is the absolute owner of the heavens and the earth, of this world and the Hereafter, and that all people will return to Him.

Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is advised to disregard them, turn away from them, and leave them to what they do. They will soon come to know their end. This is an indirect threat that suits those who, out of mere show, engage in obstinate argument and do not speak in order to establish the truth.

﴿I have come to you with wisdom﴾ (43:63). Whoever is given wisdom has, as it were, become the possessor of abundant good. He is safe from slips and deviation, protected from negligence and shortcoming, and his steps on the right path begin to fall with perfect balance and in light. Moreover, he came to them especially so that he might remove the great division that had arisen among the religious groups at that time. The jurists of the Law of Moses had begun great disagreement, and the people had split into sects and fragments. He called his people to fear Allah and obey him, and he explained the doctrine of Tawhid with great clarity, without any doubt or confusion or complexity.

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:64). He neither claimed to be a deity, nor claimed to be the son of Allah, and in his speech he did not allude anywhere to any relationship with Allah other than the relationship of Lord and servant, and of Creator and creature. He only said that he was a messenger, sent with the straight path, in which there is no crookedness, no slippage, and no deviation. Yet those who came after Jesus (peace be upon him) also became fragments and parties, just as the people before him had been fragments and parties. They created these differences merely through wrongdoing; there was neither justification for the differences nor any basis for doubt.

﴿So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65).

The mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was for the Children of Israel. In that era the Children of Israel were subjects of the Romans. They were waiting for a Redeemer who would come and free them, but when he came, they refused to recognize him, turned to enmity against him, and sought to crucify him.

When he appeared, the Children of Israel were divided into fragments, and there were four major sects:

1. The Sadducees: They were named after Sadoq; he and his family were the priests of the Temple of Solomon. From the time of David and Solomon (peace be upon them) they held this office. According to the Law, it was necessary that their lineage reach Aaron (peace be upon him), the brother of Moses (peace be upon him) and a prophet, because the descendants of Aaron alone were the custodians of the Temple. These people laid great emphasis on the outward form of worship according to their duties, and were strict opponents of any innovation, while in their personal lives they were very indulgent and enjoyed life's pleasures, and they held the belief that there is no Resurrection.

2. The Pharisees: They were strongly opposed to the Sadducees. Their objection to them was that these people laid great emphasis on the outward form of religious rites and worship and denied the Resurrection and the reckoning. They were extremely pious people of a Sufi type, although some of them were overcome by intellectual pride, and Jesus (peace be upon him) did not like their intellectual arrogance. Moreover, he did not like their verbosity either.

3. The third sect was that of the Samaritans: This sect consisted of Jews and Assyrians, and it accepted only the first five books of the Old Testament, considering the rest to be later additions. These five books are known as the Books of Moses, whereas the other sects accepted all the books.

4. They were called Essenes or Essenians: These people were influenced by certain philosophical ideas. They kept themselves separate from the other sects, and subjected themselves to great severity and asceticism, and their community was also very strict in organization.

Apart from these four well-known sects, there were also many individual sects. In short, among the Children of Israel there was severe disagreement and disintegration in their beliefs and conduct, and they were under heavy pressure from the Roman imperial power, and the whole nation was living a life of extreme humiliation and slavery. This was the setting in which a prophecy about a Redeemer had been recorded in their books, that he would come and deliver them.

When Messiah was sent with the doctrine of Tawhid and he made the proclamation:

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾ (43:63), and along with it he presented a law that emphasized compassion and spiritual reform, and stressed the spiritual aspect of worship rather than its outward form, then those jurists and Pharisees opposed him, because they laid stress only on the outward forms of worship.

Among the things Jesus (peace be upon him) said about these people, some of his statements are very effective, such as: "They bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger. But all their works they do to be seen of men... and they love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi."

And to the Pharisees and scribes he said: "Woe unto you, blind guides, which strain at a gnat and swallow a camel! You cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess... Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like unto whitewashed tombs, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones and of all uncleanness."

Read these words of Jesus (peace be upon him) and look at the scholars and muftis of your own age: do these very words not apply to them—those who distort religion, the worshippers of rituals, the outwardly pious and the showy?

After this, Jesus (peace be upon him) went to his Lord. Thereafter, differences arose among his followers. In this way they split into sects and fragments. Some made him a deity; some took him to be the son of Allah; some said "Trinity," and the word of Tawhid, for which he had come so that these people might return to their Lord and make religion pure for Allah, was lost from them.

﴿But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ (43:65). The idolaters of Arabia came and began to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Jesus (peace be upon him), because the followers of the Messiah had, after him, wrought their mischief and had fabricated countless legends about him.

**Lesson 233: At a Glance**

This is the last lesson of this surah. Its subject is also the mythical beliefs of the Arabs, that the angels are the daughters of Allah and that therefore they are worshipped. Here an argument is cited that the polytheists of Makkah used in defence of their baseless beliefs. They did not put forward this argument in search of truth. It was mere pretence and deception.

When they were told that they and the idols they worship would be fuel for Hell, the intended meaning was that the idols you worship, whether they are named after the angels or after someone else, will be there. It did not mean that those whose names you attach to the idols would also be in Hell. In short, when they were told that both the worshippers and the worshipped would be in Hell, some people cited the example of Jesus, son of Mary, since some misguided Christians worshipped him. This was merely a piece of contentious argument on their part. They then said that since the People of the Book worship Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), we are better than them, because we worship the angels. This argument was the best example of *bina' al-batil 'ala al-batil* (building falsehood upon falsehood).

For this reason, an episode from the story of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) is brought here. It explains the reality of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), what his message was, what differences existed among the Children of Israel before him, and what differences arose after him.

After this, everyone holding corrupt and polytheistic ideas is warned that the Hour will come suddenly, and then what their condition will be. Next, one of the long scenes of the Day of Resurrection is presented, in which there is a glimpse of the blessings prepared for the pious (*muttaqun*) and a glimpse of the painful punishment prepared for the criminals (*mujrimun*).

In this lesson, the Arab myth that the angels are the daughters of Allah is also refuted. Allah is free of what they attribute to Him. In this connection, some of Allah's attributes are also mentioned, and it is shown that Allah is the absolute owner of the heavens and the earth, of this world and the Hereafter, and that all people will return to Him.

Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is advised to disregard them, turn away from them, and leave them to what they do. They will soon come to know their end. This is an indirect threat that suits those who, out of mere show, engage in obstinate argument and do not speak in order to establish the truth.
