**Lesson 233: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 57 to 65**

Ibn Ishaq wrote in his *Sirah* that, as it reached me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the Sacred Precinct with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith also came and sat with them. Several other Quraysh were sitting in the assembly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith raised an objection, and the Messenger (ﷺ) silenced him. After that, he recited this verse to them:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ (21:98)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then left that assembly. Then 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari al-Tamimi came and sat down in the assembly. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, when al-Nadr ibn al-Harith stood up, the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib left. Muhammad (ﷺ) thinks that we and all our deities are fuel for Hell." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I meet him, I will argue with him. Ask Muhammad (ﷺ) whether all the deities that are worshipped will be in Hell along with their worshippers. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah, son of Mary." Al-Walid and the others in the assembly were greatly impressed by the words of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari. They thought that he had presented a strong argument and had won the debate. When this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Whoever likes to be worshipped besides Allah will indeed be in Hell along with those who worshipped him. These people are in fact worshipping Satan, who commanded them to worship these elders." At that point this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

That is, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), Prophet 'Uzayr (peace be upon him), and the other rabbis and monks who were worshipped along with them, who remained steadfast in the worship of Allah, but after their deaths people began to worship them and made them *arbab min dun Allah* (lords besides Allah). As for the statement about Jesus (peace be upon him) being worshipped besides Allah, and al-Walid and the others in the assembly being impressed by it, this verse was revealed concerning it:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people raise an outcry.﴾ (43:57)

*Yasuddun* means *yasuddun 'an amrika*, that is, they keep turning away from your call.

Allamah Zamakhshari wrote in his commentary *al-Kashshaf* that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to the Quraysh this verse:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; to it you will all be brought.﴾ (21:98)

the people of Quraysh were furious. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari asked: "Muhammad, is this ruling only about our deities and about us, or does it also apply to the other religions?" He replied: "It is for you and your deities, and for all nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have defeated you! Do you not believe that 'Isa ibn Maryam is a prophet, and that you speak well of him and his mother? You also know that the Christians worship him, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the angels are worshipped as well. If all of these are in Hell, then we are ready to go to Hell along with our deities." They laughed loudly and were delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far from it.﴾ (21:101)

And this verse was also revealed, the meaning of which is that when 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'bari cited the example of 'Isa ibn Maryam and debated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), arguing that the Christians also worship 'Isa, then suddenly your people, the Quraysh, began to raise an uproar. They did this because they were very pleased with that argument, since Za'bari had silenced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Just as sometimes people without arguments, when they lose a debate and suddenly find some argument, become very happy.

The word *yasuddun* means "to raise an uproar", but those who read it as *yasudd* (with a *damma* on the *sad*) mean that they turn away from the truth and reject it. Some have said that *yasuddun* derives from *al-sadid*, which means opposition and being cut off. *Yasuddu* and *yasuddu* both occur, just as *ya'kifu* and *ya'kufu* occur.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:58)

The meaning is: in your view, are our deities not better and superior to 'Isa (peace be upon him)? If 'Isa (peace be upon him) is fuel for Hell, then the matter of our deities is easier.

This is the narration of the author of *al-Kashshaf*. We do not know from whom he took it, but in its general content it agrees with the narration of Ibn Ishaq.

From both narrations it appears that these people, in this disputation and wrangling, relied only on outward and verbal obstinacy. For this very reason the Qur'an says:

﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (43:58)

They argue and are very skilled at criticism; they are debaters. They already know well what the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intend, but then they twist the meaning to make it fit their own aim, and then they raise objections, and they object by seizing upon the general wording of the expressions. Yet they could have derived the specific meaning from the teachings of the whole Qur'an. Such general objections are raised only by one who is not sincere, who is wholly cunning, whose thinking is not sound, who is stubborn, and who is always searching for doubts, verbal tricks, and some loophole to exploit. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) always forbade conversation that is merely show without substance, and in which the speaker always wants to make his own point prevail at any cost.

Ibn Jarir narrated through Abu Kurayb, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubadah ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, and from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out while people were engaged in disputation and argument about the Qur'an. He became extremely angry, as though vinegar had been poured on his blessed face (showing sourness of countenance). Then he said: "Do not set some parts of the Qur'an against other parts, for people went astray only when religious disputes and disagreements arose among them." After that he recited:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

There is another possibility in the interpretation of this verse.

﴿And they say: "Are our deities better, or is he?"﴾ (43:57)

Here there is an indication that, according to their mythical beliefs, they worshipped the angels, and they thought that their worship was better than the worship that the Christians offered to Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). This is because the angels, by their nature and according to their fanciful notions, are closer to Allah. Upon this, the following comment:

﴿They have cited it to you only for the sake of argument. Indeed, they are a people given to contention.﴾ (43:58)

And, as has passed earlier, this is a refutation of Ibn al-Za'bari. The meaning is that citing the worship of the Christians of the Messiah as an example is baseless here. The practice of the Christians is not a proof, because they have turned away from monotheism, just as the polytheists have turned away from monotheism. Therefore there is no difference between the two; all are misguided. Some commentators have pointed to this, and it may also be a comprehensible interpretation. After this comes a comprehensive comment about Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him):

﴿He was none other than a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (43:59)

He is not a deity to be worshipped, just as a group of Christians went astray and began to worship him. He was a servant of Allah upon whom Allah bestowed His favour. If some people have worshipped him, the fault is not his. He was given prophethood and miracles and made a sign of Allah's power for the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel should have followed him and received guidance, but they went astray.

Now the discussion turns to their beliefs concerning the angels. It is explained that the angels, like you, are creatures of Allah. If We wished, We could make the angels your successors on the earth, or make some people angels who would succeed you on the earth.

﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels among you to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ (43:60)

All these matters depend upon the will of Allah. He may do with His creation whatever He wills, but no creature can establish kinship with Allah, nor can any creature reach Allah except through the relationship of creator and creature, or of worshipped and worshipper, or of master and servant.

After this, some decisions are given concerning Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him): that he is, first, a sign of the Hour, the Hour which they deny or about whose coming they have doubt.

Both meanings are correct.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is near that the son of Mary will descend among you as a just ruler. This is an unseen matter, and it has been informed to us by the truthful and trustworthy one (ﷺ), and the Qur'an also points to it. Therefore no person can say anything else about it. Only that is the truth which has come through these two reliable sources, and for us the reliable sources until the Day of Resurrection are these alone.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 66–77:

When the good news of destruction has been given to the wrongdoers and polytheists, the wrongdoing factions (al-ahzab) who split into sects after the time of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and the wrongdoers who debated and disputed with Muhammad (ﷺ) on the basis of those factions' false beliefs, are now shown in a scene of the Day of Resurrection. In this scene, a glimpse is also shown of the believing and God-fearing (muttaqin), who will be in the gardens of Paradise with great honour.

Verses 66 to 77

The scene begins with the Resurrection arriving suddenly, when they are heedless and careless of it. They did not expect that the Resurrection would come upon them suddenly.

﴿Are they waiting for anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾ (43:66)

When it comes, it will overturn all the circumstances of this world; all worldly affairs will change, and it will be a tremendous event.

﴿On that Day, friends will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing﴾ (43:67). Their friendships, which were the source of their hostility, will turn into enmity. In this world they were a gathered band of evildoers, and in misguidance they were advisers to one another. Today they will blame one another and will be shifting the responsibility for that evil and misguidance onto each other. Once they were close companions, and today they will be quarrelling opponents. ﴿Except the God-fearing﴾ (43:67): their friendship will remain, because it was founded on guidance, on mutual sincere counsel, and in the end they will attain salvation.

Where friends quarrel and dispute, a call will come from the whole of creation, and it will come from Allah, the Most Generous, and will be for the God-fearing:

﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you today, nor shall you grieve﴾ (43:68). ﴿Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims﴾ (43:69). ﴿Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, you will be made joyful﴾ (43:70). That is, you will be so happy that joy and delight will cover your sides and faces, so that you will appear as though a beautiful cloak has been spread over you.

Now our imagination sees something else, even more wondrous. Dishes and cups of gold and silver are being carried around them. Then we see that in Paradise there is for them what their souls desire and what the eyes delight in, and all these banquets will be for the sake of their utmost honour and dignity.

﴿Dishes of gold and cups will be passed around them, and therein is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in﴾ (43:71).

And beyond these blessings there is something greater and more excellent: that Allah Himself will address them and honour them, and this will be a very great distinction.

﴿And you will abide therein eternally﴾ (43:71). ﴿That is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do﴾ (43:72). ﴿For you therein is abundant fruit from which you will eat﴾ (43:73). You now remain here forever; you have inherited this Paradise because of your deeds which you did in the world. There is abundant fruit here for you, which you will eat.

This is the real reason: their dislike and aversion to the truth prevented them from accepting it. It was not that they were unable to recognise the truth. They had no doubt at all about the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They had never seen a lie attributed to him. When a person does not deal falsely with people, how could he fabricate lies against his Allah? And how could a liar claim prophethood?

Whoever wages war against the truth in this world is not ignorant of the truth. The real matter is that they do not like the truth, because the truth stands against their carnal desires and clashes with their appetites, and such people are morally so weak that they cannot suppress their desires and needs. In contrast, they are very quick to strike at the truth, and the proponents of the truth become their sworn enemies. Their weakness before the truth, and before their own desires and cravings, becomes the means by which they use force against the truth and its bearers. Then the Possessor of true power, the Almighty and Irresistible, also threatens them, declaring that He is aware of all their secret and open plots.

﴿Or do they intend a plot? Then it is We who are the plotters.﴾ (43:79) ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private consultations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing.﴾ (43:80)

Do they insist on falsehood against the truth? Then Allah also insists that He will make the truth prevail over their falsehood. Against their schemes and plots, the knowledge of Allah is at work, which knows the secret and is also aware of private consultations. Allah is the Creator, the Mighty, the All-Knowing, and those who oppose Him are weak human beings, so they will be unable to do anything.

﴾﴾﴾﴾

Leaving aside this frightening warning, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is directed to a final word: that he should say this to them, and then leave them to their own state, so that they reach the end whose picture you have just seen.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 43, verses 81–83:

Verses 81 to 83

These people worshipped the angels on the notion that they are the daughters of Allah. If Allah had offspring, then the one who would have the first right to know Him and to worship Him would be the Prophet. For among mankind, it is the Prophets and Messengers who are nearest to God. Moreover, in worship and obedience to Allah, they are the foremost of all. And if there were any offspring, the Prophets would also be the first to honour it. Therefore, this notion and assertion of theirs is nothing but fable. There is no proof for it. And it is not befitting of Allah to be attributed with such qualities; He is pure.

﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they attribute to Him﴾ (43:82). When a person reflects upon these heavens and the earth, upon their system, and sees the extreme harmony in their movement and their signs, and when he observes the greatness of the lofty and mighty power behind this system, and then observes its dominion and control over this whole system, which is indicated by the word "Lord of the Throne," then such fabulous thoughts and absurdities automatically vanish from his mind. And the person who reflects, through his own nature, comes to know that such a Being can only be unique. There can be no likeness to Him, as created beings have offspring and lineages continue. This is not fitting for Allah. He is free from it. These beliefs, after such reflection, automatically appear to be vain. They are idle talk and an unwarranted audacity. Therefore, speaking about them is itself futile. It is appropriate to leave such people to their own state.

﴿So leave them to plunge in their vain talk and to play until they encounter their Day which they are promised﴾ (43:83). A picture of what that day will be like they have already seen.

This passage is the commentary on verses 84–86 of Surah Az-Zukhruf (43) in Sayyid Qutb's Fi Zilal al-Quran, so I'll translate it as given.

After leaving these people to their own condition, some words of praise and glorification of Allah are mentioned, to show what the Lord of this great universe is like. These are His attributes:

Verses 84 to 86

This is the proclamation that in the heavens and the earth there is only one divinity (uluhiyyah), who is unique and has no partner. Whatever He does, He does with wisdom, and He acts in accordance with His all-encompassing knowledge. Then the word tabaraka is used here, meaning He is full of blessings, and He is far exalted above the conceptions these people hold about Him. He is the Lord and Owner of the heavens and the earth and of all creatures within them. He alone is the knower of the Day of Judgment, and to Him is the return. On that day, none of those gods will be present; all of them will be absent, those whom these people call upon. For these people used to say, "These lords of ours are in truth our intercessors," whereas intercession will avail only the one to whom permission has been granted in advance; and clearly, those who are granted such permission will not intercede for the opponents of the truth and the enemies of Islam.

Now, before them is set the matter about which they neither doubted nor disputed: that Allah alone is our Creator. The question is put to them: when Allah is the Creator, why then do you associate others with Allah?

Verse 87

That is, why do they turn away from the truth which their own nature acknowledges, and go off in another direction?

At the close of the surah, the complaint of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is brought forward, which he would make: that my people are set upon disbelief, obstinacy and refusal to believe. Here that complaint is brought forward and an oath is sworn upon it.

This manner of expression shows that this supplication (complaint) reaches far, that its consequences will be profound, that it has been heard, and that the higher realm is taking some great steps as a result of it. Therefore, O Prophet (ﷺ), leave them to their own condition, pay no heed to their activities and intrigues, remain content, and continue on your path with complete peace, safety and nobility.

In this too there is a severe warning, though veiled, to those who do not believe. It concerns the Day when all secrets will be made manifest.

"So turn away from them and say, 'Peace,' for they will come to know."
